CareWatch: Project Master Guide

A complete learning and viva-preparation guide for the U.S. nursing-home quality warehouse (CMS data → Bronze → Silver → Gold → Power BI) on Databricks, PySpark and Delta Lake.

Hassan Mehmood · BDS-5BTeam: Hassan Mehmood, Hanan IshaqBuilt from repository HEAD d8a6807 · 15 Nov 2026Fully offline · no external requests

Use the sidebar to jump, press / to search, open any block to read it, and tick the checklists as you master each step. Sections: A overview · B architecture · C learning path · D files · E code walkthroughs · F record trace · G database and Power BI · H requirements · I evidence · J decisions · K demo guide · L what not to claim · M viva Q&A · N study plan.

Nothing in this guide was run on Databricks or against remote data. Numbers marked ACTUAL come from the repository or from local files; DOCUMENTED ones come from the project's own evidence; anything not available is marked NOT AVAILABLE.

A · Project overview

What CareWatch is, what it does end to end, and the 60-second version you can say to an examiner.

What the project is

CareWatch is a data-engineering and BI project about the quality and regulatory record of Medicare/Medicaid-certified U.S. nursing homes. It pulls four public datasets from the CMS Provider Data Catalog, moves them through a Bronze → Silver → Gold Medallion lakehouse with PySpark and Delta Lake on Databricks, and serves a Power BI dashboard. It is decision support, not medical advice (README).

The common join key across all four datasets is the 6-character facility id, cms_certification_number_ccn (the CCN). The team is Hassan Mehmood (24L2559) and Hanan Ishaq (24L2537), BDS-5B.

How data flows (one paragraph)

  1. Acquire (01_acquire_cms): bulk CSVs are streamed from the CMS download URL (SHA-256 while streaming, atomic rename); API data is fetched in 500-row pages for a date window. Every file is registered in source_file_manifest.
  2. Raw → Bronze (02_raw_to_bronze): only manifest-registered files are read, with explicit all-string schemas. Added columns evolve the table, missing columns reject the file, corrupt rows go to bronze_quarantine. After a whole acquisition run reconciles, the watermark advances.
  3. Bronze → Silver (03_bronze_to_silver): trim, safe-cast, validate, hash keys and the address (salted), drop phone/address/location, de-duplicate, quarantine rejects, and MERGE by entity key.
  4. Silver → Gold (04_silver_to_gold): build five dimensions, three facts and a state-month aggregate from the complete current Silver state, validate, then nine hash-aware MERGEs.
  5. BI: Power BI reads Gold tables and two monitoring views through a Databricks SQL warehouse.

The 60-second examiner script

Say this (≈ 60 seconds, about 150 words)

“CareWatch is an end-to-end lakehouse pipeline for U.S. nursing-home quality. We take four public CMS datasets: provider information, health deficiencies, penalties and MDS quality measures, joined on the facility CCN. A daily Databricks Job runs four notebooks in order: acquire, raw-to-Bronze, Bronze-to-Silver, Silver-to-Gold. Bronze keeps everything as strings with lineage. Silver types, validates, hashes keys and the address with a secret salt, quarantines bad rows and uses Delta MERGE so reruns create no duplicates. Gold is a star schema: five dimensions, three facts and one aggregate, validated before a hash-aware MERGE. Every step is audited in pipeline_execution_logs, which also feeds a Pipeline Health page in Power BI. The 25 October scheduled run took 489 seconds and cost about 48 cents of Databricks list price.”

If you only have 20 seconds

“Four CMS datasets → Bronze (raw strings) → Silver (typed, validated, hashed, MERGE) → Gold (star schema) → Power BI, orchestrated by one daily Databricks Job, with audit logging and quarantine throughout.”

Two honesty rules used throughout

Nothing here was run on Databricks: no remote or write operation was executed to produce this guide. Where a number cannot be found in the repo it says NOT AVAILABLE; it is never guessed.

Why the control tables matter

Notebooks 02 and 03 never list folders or compare timestamps. They ask these tables what is pending. That is the entire basis of idempotent reruns, safe retries and backfills.

Honest limits of the architecture (say them before they are asked)
  • Not atomic across Gold. Nine MERGEs commit separately; the design validates before and after (README says so too).
  • Clear-text PII in Bronze and landing. Telephone and address exist in the landing files and Bronze; they are dropped or hashed only at Silver.
  • SCD Type 1 only. There is no history of provider profile changes; the proposal's fact_facility_snapshot was deliberately not built (README).

Checklist

Dependency picture

config → schemas → audit → (acquire, watermarks) → (drift → bronze) → silver → gold → job → Power BI. A function from a later module may call an earlier one, never the reverse; gold.py reuses silver.sha256_json_columns to build the same facility key as Silver.

E1 · Foundation, audit and acquisition

CRITICAL Dataset registry & safe naming — config.py · src/carewatch/config.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

DatasetConfig is a frozen dataclass; DATASETS registers the four CMS feeds with their CMS dataset id, incremental strategy (api_date_window or snapshot_diff), watermark column, history start date, Bronze/Silver table names and business-key columns. get_dataset() and qualified_name() are the two helpers every other module uses.

Every acquisition, Bronze and Silver loop iterates this registry, so adding a feed is one entry and not scattered if statements. qualified_name() validates catalog, schema and object names against ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ before they are pasted into DDL/SQL strings, which blocks malformed or hostile widget input.

2a · Inputs
  • A dataset name string from a widget (health_deficiencies, penalties, provider_info, mds_quality).
  • Catalog, schema and object name strings for qualified_name.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • A DatasetConfig object, or ValueError listing the allowed names.
  • A dotted three-part name such as carewatch.pipeline.silver_deficiency, or ValueError.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. At import time Python builds the immutable DATASETS dictionary once.
  2. get_dataset(name) does a dictionary lookup; a miss raises ValueError that lists the valid names.
  3. qualified_name(catalog, schema, object) tests every part with the identifier regex.
  4. If any part is unsafe it raises; otherwise it joins the parts with dots.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 14–25The registry entry type. frozen=True makes instances immutable so no notebook can mutate shared configuration by accident. watermark_col and history_start_date are None for snapshot-style feeds.
lines 29–45Deficiencies: CMS id r5ix-sfxw, refreshed through the CMS datastore API in date windows on survey_date; history starts 2017-03-23; Bronze bronze_nh_health_deficiencies, Silver silver_deficiency.
lines 62–70Provider information: refreshed by comparing newly published bulk CSV snapshots (snapshot_diff), so there is no watermark column and no history start. Its only business key is the CCN, and it lands in silver_facility.
lines 90–110get_dataset turns a bad widget value into a readable error. qualified_name is the injection guard: names are validated, then joined. All DDL in 00_setup_tables, audit.ensure_delta_table and the Gold views goes through it.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • Standard library only: re, dataclasses, datetime.date, typing.Literal.

Called by: acquire.py, bronze.py, silver.py, gold.py, audit.py, watermarks (via notebooks) and all five pipeline notebooks.

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • Defines the loop for config in DATASETS.values() used by notebook 01 and the dataset widgets in 02/03.
  • incremental_strategy decides in acquire_dataset whether to call the bulk or the API acquirer.
  • watermark_col decides whether reconcile_acquisition_run commits a watermark.
  • bronze_table and silver_table name the Delta tables each stage writes.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ACTUAL

For health_deficiencies the registry says: CMS id r5ix-sfxw, API window on survey_date, Bronze table bronze_nh_health_deficiencies, Silver silver_deficiency. qualified_name('carewatch','pipeline','silver_deficiency') returns carewatch.pipeline.silver_deficiency; a widget value such as pipeline; DROP TABLE x (illustrative bad input) would raise ValueError before reaching SQL.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“config.py is our dataset registry. Everything else is driven from it: how a dataset is refreshed, which column is its watermark, and the Bronze/Silver table names. qualified_name validates identifiers so a widget value can never inject SQL.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Delete or rename a DATASETS entry: notebook 01 stops acquiring that feed and 02/03 reject the widget value.
  • Change incremental_strategy: acquire_dataset switches between API-window and bulk-snapshot paths.
  • Weaken the regex: names containing quotes/semicolons could reach f-string DDL.
  • Note: key_cols and history_start_date are not read by any pipeline code in the current tree (checked by search); they are documentation/reserved values. Silver keys really come from schemas.SILVER_BUSINESS_KEYS.
CRITICAL Execution audit log — audit.audited() and LOG_SCHEMA · src/carewatch/audit.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

audited() is a context manager wrapped around one unit of work (a file, a batch, the Gold refresh). It builds a log record with zeros and SUCCESS, lets the caller fill row counts, then in a finally block stamps end time and appends one row to pipeline_execution_logs. If the body raises, it sets FAILURE, stores the truncated message and re-raises.

The assignment requires pipeline_execution_logs. More importantly, the log is a control table: Raw-to-Bronze and Bronze-to-Silver decide what is still pending by reading it. So one wrapper guarantees every attempt, success or failure, leaves an auditable row.

2a · Inputs
  • spark, the fully qualified log table name, a run_id (UUID of this notebook run), layer name, dataset, load type, a human-readable parameter string, optional batch_id and pipeline_run_id.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • Yields a mutable record dict to the caller.
  • Appends one validated row to pipeline_execution_logs (explicit LOG_SCHEMA, never inferred).
  • Status becomes QUARANTINED_PARTIAL when rows_quarantined > 0 on a success path, FAILURE on exception.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Create the record with start_time=utc_now(), status SUCCESS and all counters 0.
  2. yield record — the caller runs the real work and updates counters.
  3. After a clean body: if rows_quarantined > 0 and status is still SUCCESS, flip to QUARANTINED_PARTIAL.
  4. On Exception: set FAILURE, store truncate_error(exc) (max 2,000 characters), re-raise.
  5. In finally: stamp end_time and load_timestamp; if suppress_audit_log was used and there was no error, return without logging.
  6. Otherwise write_execution_log validates (layer, load type, status, non-negative integer counters) and appends. If that write fails while a processing error already exists, print a warning so the original error is not masked.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 24–36The closed vocabularies. The four layers match the four pipeline stages; _validate_log_record rejects anything else.
lines 181–203Guard before every write: unknown layer/load type/status is a programming error; every metric must be a non-negative int (booleans rejected); only rows_aggregated may be None.
lines 222–230Adds defaults for the two Phase 3 columns, truncates the error, validates, and appends with the explicit schema. This is where the “no inferSchema” rule is honoured for control tables.
lines 292–322Builds the record up front. Every counter starts at 0 so a failure still has a complete row; the notebook updates counters inside the with body.
lines 323–331The core state machine: run the body (yield), flip to QUARANTINED_PARTIAL if rows were quarantined, or mark FAILURE with the error text.
lines 333–347Always runs. It stamps times, honours the “no-op” suppression marker (only when no error), writes the log, and never lets a failing log write hide the real exception.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • utc_now, truncate_error, write_execution_log, _validate_log_record, append_typed_records.
  • Spark: createDataFrame(rows, schema=LOG_SCHEMA).write.format('delta').mode('append').

Called by: Notebooks 02 (per file), 03 (per Bronze batch) and 04 (Gold refresh). Notebook 01 builds records directly with completed_log_record.

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • select_silver_work_items joins to this table to skip batches that already have a terminal Silver log (SUCCESS/QUARANTINED_PARTIAL).
  • _successful_bronze_batch_ids and find_*_api_window read it to know whether Bronze finished.
  • vw_gold_pipeline_runs / vw_gold_errors expose it to Power BI's Pipeline Health page.
  • pipeline_run_id ties the four tasks of one Job run together.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ACTUAL

In the saved Pipeline Health screenshot a Bronze-to-Silver deficiency row shows QUARANTINED_PARTIAL with rows_read=418,947 and rows_quarantined=36. That is exactly this logic: Silver accepted 418,911 rows, rejected 36, so audited flipped SUCCESS to QUARANTINED_PARTIAL.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“Every unit of work runs inside audited(). It logs one row whether it succeeds or fails, flips to QUARANTINED_PARTIAL if rows were rejected, and re-raises errors. The log is also our checkpoint table, so retries only pick up work that has no terminal log yet.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Remove it: no audit rows, so Silver would reprocess every batch each run and the Pipeline Health page would be empty; the rubric's logging requirement fails.
  • Change the status vocabulary without updating VALID_STATUSES: _validate_log_record raises.
  • Re-raise removed: failures would be logged but the notebook would carry on and the Job would not fail.
  • Note: Python 3.14 prints a SyntaxWarning for the return inside finally (the repo's __pycache__ shows CPython 3.12, where it is silent). Behaviour is correct because that return runs only when there is no processing error.
CRITICAL Control tables & setup — audit.ensure_delta_table / ensure_control_tables · src/carewatch/audit.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

Defines the explicit StructType schemas for six control tables (pipeline_execution_logs, source_file_manifest, ingestion_watermarks, schema_drift_log, bronze_quarantine, silver_quarantine) and the functions that create them or verify an existing one. ensure_delta_table either checks the existing schema matches exactly or issues CREATE TABLE … USING DELTA with NOT NULL constraints.

The pipeline is safe to rerun only if its control tables have the contract the code expects. A silently different table (wrong type, missing column) would corrupt checkpoints. Failing closed on mismatch is cheaper than debugging bad state later. DDL is used (not an empty DataFrame write) because empty DataFrame writes can lose nullable=False in Unity Catalog.

2a · Inputs
  • spark, catalog, schema_name; for Silver/Gold tables, a StructType from schemas.py or gold.py.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • Delta tables created if missing; for existing tables an action string VERIFIED, CREATED or LEGACY_SCHEMA_ACCEPTED_NO_MIGRATION.
  • Additive ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMNS migrations for older manifest/watermark/drift tables.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. ensure_control_tables loops over CONTROL_TABLE_SCHEMAS.
  2. For silver_quarantine, an old five-column table is accepted but never altered (setup refuses to migrate).
  3. For manifest / watermarks / drift tables, missing legacy columns are added with ALTER TABLE (and back-filled for as_of_date).
  4. Each table then goes through ensure_delta_table: compare name→type signatures; mismatch or unexpected column raises ValueError; no table means build a column list from the schema and run CREATE TABLE.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 39–60The log contract. Business columns are non-nullable; the two Phase 3 additions pipeline_run_id and rows_aggregated are nullable at the end so older rows (written before Phase 3) remain valid.
lines 161–168The registry of six control tables that setup creates/verifies.
lines 378–408Exact-match verification (extra or retyped columns raise) or CREATE TABLE with explicit NOT NULL. The comment in the code explains why DDL is used.
lines 411–436Loops the registry; legacy five-column silver_quarantine is tolerated but never changed from setup.
lines 437–480Additive migrations only (ADD COLUMNS, one back-filling UPDATE); nothing is dropped or recreated, preserving audit history.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • spark.catalog.tableExists, spark.table(...).schema, spark.sql('ALTER/CREATE TABLE …').
  • config.qualified_name for the table names.

Called by: Notebook 00_setup_tables (all tables), notebook 02 (control tables, cheap re-check), and 03 (via silver_quarantine_schema_state).

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • Notebook 00 uses ensure_delta_table also for the 4 Silver and 9 Gold tables (schemas from schemas.py / gold.py).
  • Silver processing requires silver_quarantine to be CURRENT (eight columns) and refuses to run on LEGACY.
  • README’s Phase 3 deployment note says to ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMNS (pipeline_run_id, rows_aggregated) once before first running updated setup.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ACTUAL

Setup run on a fresh carewatch.pipeline: all six control tables are CREATED; running it again returns VERIFIED for each. The saved 11 Oct validation shows SHOW TABLES IN carewatch.pipeline returning all four Bronze, four Silver and the control tables.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“Setup is declarative and fail-closed. Every table has an explicit schema in code; setup creates it or verifies the existing table matches exactly, and only does additive migrations so audit history is never lost.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Remove ensure_delta_table: schema mismatches would only surface later as Spark write errors.
  • Switch to dropping/recreating on mismatch: you would lose audit history and watermarks, so incremental runs would fail.
  • Change LOG_SCHEMA without migrating the deployed table: 00_setup_tables raises with a precise mismatch dictionary.
CRITICAL Acquisition dispatcher & bulk snapshot — acquire_dataset / _acquire_bulk_snapshot · src/carewatch/acquire.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

acquire_dataset chooses the acquisition strategy from the request and registry. Full loads and snapshot-diff feeds call _acquire_bulk_snapshot, which reads the CMS catalog item, resolves the official CSV downloadURL, skips unchanged publications, streams the file to the Volume with a SHA-256, compares to the datastore row count, and returns a manifest-ready record. This module has no Spark dependency.

The brief required full loads to be fetched inside Databricks (not uploaded manually). Hashing and recording the publication key lets the pipeline avoid downloading the same CMS publication twice and prove later that the file was not altered.

2a · Inputs
  • AcquisitionRequest (dataset, load_type, as_of_date, landing_root, overlap, force_refresh, run id).
  • Dictionaries of already landed content hashes and prior bulk publications (built in notebook 01 from the manifest).
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • An AcquisitionResult containing one AcquiredFile (status SUCCESS or SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED).
  • A new file at <landing_root>/full_load|incremental/<dataset>/<as_of_date>/<run_id>/<name>_<sha12>.csv unless skipped.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Fetch catalog item JSON; pick the CSV distribution URL; read its modified date.
  2. Build publication_key = '<modified>|<url>'; if a prior manifest row exists, its file still exists and force_refresh is false → return SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED without downloading.
  3. Otherwise stream the file to a hidden .partial temp name while hashing it.
  4. Ask the datastore API for the dataset’s row count (reconciliation anchor).
  5. If identical content already exists in the manifest → drop the temp file and reuse the path; else atomically rename it to its final hashed name.
  6. Create the AcquiredFile with deterministic batch_id; always delete the temp file in finally.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 233–237The deterministic batch id: SHA-256 of dataset|load_type|source_identity|digest, first 24 hex chars. The same content always gets the same id, which is the foundation of idempotent Bronze replacement.
lines 342–346Resolve the official bulk CSV from CMS metadata and compute the publication key used to detect an unchanged release.
lines 347–395Skip path: if the same publication was landed before and its file still exists, reuse it, copy the previous hash/size/row facts, and mark SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED. No bytes are downloaded.
lines 397–402New release: stream into a unique .partial file so a crashed download can never look like a finished file.
lines 404–418Fetch the authoritative row count; if the byte content hash is already known, discard the duplicate; otherwise rename atomically (os.replace) to a name containing the first 12 hash characters.
lines 420–452Record everything Bronze will need: path, SHA-256, size, expected_run_rows; source_rows stays None until Bronze parses the file and row_count_validated stays false.
lines 454–456Cleanup always runs, even after a failed count check.
lines 250–292Download integrity: Accept-Encoding: identity, 1 MB chunks hashed while written, empty file rejected, and a short read versus declared Content-Length rejected (3 retries with exponential back-off).
lines 654–686The dispatcher: full → bulk snapshot; incremental + snapshot_diff → bulk snapshot with strategy label snapshot_diff; otherwise API window.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • get_catalog_item, select_csv_distribution, bulk_publication_key, get_dataset_count, _stream_to_temporary_file, _batch_id, _landing_directory.
  • requests with a custom User-Agent; hashlib, os.replace.

Called by: Notebook 01_acquire_cms through acquire_dataset.

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • The result becomes a row in source_file_manifest plus a CMS-to-Landing log row (notebook 01).
  • batch_id and source_file_sha256 are verified again by Bronze (verify_landing_file).
  • expected_run_rows is what reconcile_acquisition_run later compares with parsed rows.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ACTUAL

The 25 Oct 2026 scheduled run acquired one health_deficiencies item while provider and MDS snapshots were “already acquired” (per spark_finops_2026-10-25.md): that is the SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED path for the two snapshot-diff datasets.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“For full loads and snapshot feeds we discover the CSV URL from the CMS catalog, stream it with a SHA-256, and compare against the API row count. If CMS has not published anything new we skip the download. The batch id is a hash of dataset, load type, URL and content, so the same input always yields the same id.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Remove the SHA-256: Bronze could no longer detect a changed landing file, and duplicate detection by content fails.
  • Remove the .partial rename: an interrupted download could be registered as complete.
  • Change _batch_id: the same file gets a new id, so replaceWhere replacement and idempotent reprocessing no longer line up with historical logs.
  • Drop the publication-key skip: every daily run re-downloads ~hundreds of MB for unchanged provider/MDS data (higher cost).
CRITICAL API date-window acquisition — _acquire_api_window · src/carewatch/acquire.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

For Health Deficiencies and Penalties it pages the CMS datastore API for rows whose watermark column falls in [window_start, as_of_date], 500 rows per page. Each page is written as a JSON envelope file, and the page list becomes the manifest rows of one acquisition run.

Incrementals must be small and replayable. The window start is the last Bronze-committed watermark minus a 60-day overlap, so late CMS corrections are picked up again (Bronze keeps batches; Silver MERGE makes the overlap harmless). Strict validation (count drift, repeated pages, final count) protects against a changing or paged-wrong API feed.

2a · Inputs
  • AcquisitionRequest, the dataset config, last_successful_watermark, existing content hashes.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • One part-<offset>-<hash12>.json per page under the landing directory.
  • An AcquisitionResult with one AcquiredFile per page, each carrying expected_run_rows, page_offset, window_start/end.
  • On any exception: all files created in this attempt are deleted.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Resolve window_start (explicit date, or watermark − overlap; refuse if no watermark).
  2. Loop: fetch page at offset; reject a missing results array; check the reported total did not change between pages.
  3. Hash the page; a page identical to an earlier page in this run is rejected (API repeated itself).
  4. Wrap results in a _meta envelope; compute a content hash (window + offset + rows) and a file hash.
  5. Reuse an existing identical file or write atomically; build the AcquiredFile with status SUCCESS/SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED.
  6. Stop when a page has fewer than 500 rows; verify the total fetched equals the reported count; on error clean up the created files.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 119–133The watermark rule in one function: explicit start wins; no watermark means the incremental cannot start (the error text sends you to the full load); otherwise start = watermark − overlap days.
lines 459–483The CMS datastore query: conditions[0] is watermark_col >= window_start, conditions[1] is <= window_end, with limit/offset paging and count=true so the total is returned.
lines 496–512Set-up: compute the window, refuse an inverted window, prepare the list of files created (for cleanup), the repeated-page detector and the human filter text stored in each envelope.
lines 516–532Fetch one page and enforce a stable total count across all pages of the run.
lines 534–539Repeated-page detector: if CMS returns the same non-empty page twice, the pagination is unreliable and the run fails.
lines 541–566Build the landing file: envelope with _meta (dataset, filter, rows_available, rows_in_file) and results; content_digest identifies window+offset+rows (stable across runs) while file_digest hashes the bytes including fetch time.
lines 568–579Reuse an identical page already on disk, or write atomically and remember the created path for rollback.
lines 581–609Each page becomes a manifest-ready AcquiredFile with row_count_validated=False; Bronze will set source_rows after parsing.
lines 619–630End of data (short page), final count reconciliation, and cleanup of this attempt’s files on any exception.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • resolve_window_start, _query_api_page, _get_json (4 retries, 2^n back-off), _write_json_atomic, _sha256_file, _batch_id.

Called by: acquire_dataset when incremental_strategy == 'api_date_window' and load_type == 'incremental'.

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • Notebook 01 first asks find_complete_api_window whether the exact window was already acquired, and find_pending_api_window whether an earlier complete acquisition is still waiting for Bronze.
  • Bronze validate_json_envelope re-checks the _meta values; reconcile_acquisition_run re-checks contiguous 500-row offsets.
  • The Bronze watermark commit uses the window end (as_of_date) of this run.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ILLUSTRATIVE

Penalties watermark = 2026-10-24 (illustrative value), overlap 60, as_of 2026-10-25 → window 2026-08-25..2026-10-25. CMS reports count=300, so one page file part-000000000-<hash12>.json with rows_in_file=300 is written; because 300 < 500 the loop ends and acquired_rows == expected_rows. Real run evidence (25 Oct): the scheduled run acquired one health_deficiencies item.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“Incrementals ask the CMS API for rows in a date window starting at our last committed watermark minus 60 days. We page 500 rows at a time, reject any page that repeats or any total that changes, and only advance the watermark later, after Bronze has loaded and reconciled every page.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Remove the overlap: late corrections to old rows would never be re-read.
  • Remove the repeated-page / count-drift checks: an unstable API could silently lose or duplicate rows (offset paging can race a changing feed — still a known limitation, see section L).
  • Advance the watermark at acquisition time instead of Bronze commit: a failure after download would skip data permanently.
  • Remove the cleanup: partial landing files from a failed run would remain with misleading manifest-free paths.
CRITICAL Watermarks & window state — watermarks.py · src/carewatch/watermarks.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

Reads and advances the per-dataset extraction checkpoint in ingestion_watermarks, and decides from the manifest and the log whether an API window is already acquired (find_complete_api_window) or acquired-but-not-yet-in-Bronze (find_pending_api_window).

A watermark that moves too early loses data; one that never moves re-reads everything. This module makes the rule explicit: only Bronze, after reconciliation, may advance it, and only monotonically (a stale retry cannot move it backwards).

2a · Inputs
  • spark, manifest, log and watermark table names, dataset, window dates.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • AcquisitionWindowState objects (run id, batch ids, landing paths, expected/acquired rows, bronze_complete) or None.
  • A MERGE into ingestion_watermarks.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. _complete_window_state takes all manifest rows of one acquisition run and returns a state only if: one expected count, every page parsed, parsed total equals expected, all statuses successful, page offsets exactly 0, 500, 1000…, and every landing file still exists.
  2. It also checks the log to see whether every batch already has a successful Raw-to-Bronze row (bronze_complete).
  3. find_complete_api_window scans manifest runs for the exact window dates, newest first.
  4. find_pending_api_window scans runs whose window end is newer than the committed watermark and returns one that is complete but not yet in Bronze.
  5. commit_bronze_watermark MERGEs one row per dataset, updating only when source.watermark_value >= target.watermark_value.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 95–103Completeness test part 1: exactly one authoritative expected row count; every page must have a parsed source_rows.
lines 105–120Completeness test part 2: parsed total equals expected, statuses successful, offsets contiguous in 500-row steps, files present on disk.
lines 124–137Bronze completeness is derived from successful Raw-to-Bronze log rows, again using logs as checkpoints.
lines 155–189Exact-window lookup: filter manifest rows to this dataset/strategy/dates, group by acquisition run (newest first) and return the first run that passes the completeness test.
lines 266–287The monotonic MERGE: insert if first time; update only when the incoming date is not older, so a stale retry can never move the checkpoint backwards.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • table_exists, read_successful_watermark, _bronze_success_batch_ids, _complete_window_state.
  • Delta DeltaTable.forName(...).merge(...); audit.WATERMARK_SCHEMA.

Called by: Notebook 01 (read_successful_watermark, find_*), and bronze.reconcile_acquisition_run (commit_bronze_watermark).

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • Notebook 01 raises if an incremental run is requested but an API dataset has no watermark (the initial full load through Bronze must happen first).
  • Full-load reconciliation of an event dataset sets the watermark to the load’s as_of_date, which seeds later incremental windows.
  • Silver never calls the watermark function (README and design notes: Silver does not advance extraction checkpoints).
7 · Realistic project-specific example ILLUSTRATIVE

After the initial full load of penalties on 2026-10-09 (illustrative date), the watermark row is penalties | penalty_date | 2026-10-09. Tomorrow’s incremental window starts 60 days earlier. If Bronze fails on one page of today’s run, find_pending_api_window returns that complete-but-unloaded run and notebook 01 refuses to acquire another window until 02_raw_to_bronze is run.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“The watermark is a checkpoint that only Bronze can advance, and only after the whole acquisition run is parsed and its row counts reconcile. The MERGE only updates when the new date is greater or equal, so a retry can never move it backwards.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Let acquisition advance the watermark: a download that never reached Bronze would permanently skip rows.
  • Remove the >= guard: an old retry could regress the watermark and trigger repeated reprocessing.
  • Remove the contiguous-offset test: a missing page in the middle would go unnoticed.
  • Delete find_pending_api_window: you could acquire a second window while the first is stuck, leaving a hole.
CRITICAL Orchestration notebook 01 — acquire CMS · notebooks/01_acquire_cms.ipynb
1 · What it does and why it exists

The thin Databricks notebook that, for every dataset, builds an AcquisitionRequest, reuses an already acquired exact API window if there is one, otherwise calls acquire_dataset, appends manifest and CMS-to-Landing log rows, and finally raises if any dataset failed.

Business logic lives in src/carewatch/; the notebook only wires widgets, Spark tables and the loop. A failure in one dataset must not hide another dataset’s result, so errors are collected and raised only after all four have been attempted.

2a · Inputs
  • Widgets load_type (full/incremental), overlap_days (60), force_refresh, catalog, schema, landing_root, pipeline_run_id (set by the Job to {{job.run_id}}).
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • Landing files in the Volume.
  • Appended rows in source_file_manifest and pipeline_execution_logs (layer CMS-to-Landing, statuses SUCCESS, SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED or FAILURE).
  • RuntimeError listing failed datasets (so the Job task fails).
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Cell 0–1: add src/ to sys.path, import modules, declare widgets.
  2. Cell 2: as_of_date = today UTC; helper functions build existing_content_files and existing_bulk_publications from the manifest.
  3. Cell 3: for incremental runs read the Bronze watermarks of the two API datasets and raise if any is missing.
  4. Loop each dataset: for API datasets compute window_start, skip if find_complete_api_window says it is already acquired (writes SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED logs), raise if find_pending_api_window finds unloaded data.
  5. Call acquire_dataset; append manifest records and one log row per file.
  6. On exception: record the failure, write a FAILURE log, continue to the next dataset.
  7. Cell 4: display a summary and raise RuntimeError if any dataset failed.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
cell 3, lines 4–20Incremental guard: read the committed Bronze watermark for each API dataset; if one is missing the run stops before any download.
cell 3, lines 22–38The per-dataset loop starts; last_watermark is only used for API datasets in incremental mode.
cell 3, lines 47–85Reuse path: if the exact window is already complete in the manifest, write SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED logs per batch and move on — no API calls.
cell 3, lines 86–96Gate: a newer complete acquisition still waiting for Bronze blocks another acquisition.
cell 3, lines 98–113The real acquisition call with the reuse dictionaries; then the manifest append with the explicit schema.
cell 3, lines 146–178Failure handling: remember the error, try to write a FAILURE log, and continue with the other datasets.
cell 4, lines 16–19End of notebook: raising makes the Databricks task fail, so ALL_SUCCESS stops tasks 2–4.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • acquire.acquire_dataset, AcquisitionRequest, bulk_publication_key, parse_bool.
  • audit.completed_log_record, append_typed_records, write_execution_log, LOG_SCHEMA, MANIFEST_SCHEMA.
  • watermarks.find_complete_api_window, find_pending_api_window, read_successful_watermark, table_exists.
6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • First task of the Job; outputs feed 02_raw_to_bronze through the manifest.
  • pipeline_run_id stamps the logs so the Pipeline Health page and Gold audit can be tied to one Job run.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ACTUAL

25 Oct 2026 scheduled run: acquisition took 103 s; one deficiencies item was downloaded, provider/MDS were already acquired (evidence file spark_finops_2026-10-25.md).

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“Notebook 01 is only orchestration. For each dataset it decides: skip, reuse, or acquire. It records everything in the manifest and the logs, continues past a failed dataset so we see all failures, and then raises so the Job stops downstream tasks.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Remove the final raise: downstream tasks would run after a failed download.
  • Remove the watermark guard: incremental resolve_window_start would raise later with a less helpful stack.
  • Skip the manifest append: Bronze finds no work (it only reads manifest rows).

E2 · Drift detection and Raw-to-Bronze

CRITICAL Schema-drift classification — drift.classify_csv_header / classify_json_keys + bronze._drift_records · src/carewatch/drift.py + src/carewatch/bronze.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

classify_csv_header compares the physical header of a landed CSV with the expected source columns and returns a DriftAssessment: the ordered Bronze column names, which expected columns are missing, which new columns were added, and which are invalid or duplicate. classify_json_keys does the same for CMS API pages. bronze._drift_records converts the assessment into rows for schema_drift_log.

CMS renames and adds fields. The assignment asks for schema-evolution handling with a log. The design here is: compatible change (a new column) is accepted and logged, breaking change (a required column missing, an unsafe/reserved/duplicate name) is logged and the file is rejected before any Bronze write.

2a · Inputs
  • The physical header (tuple of strings) from read_csv_header, or the union of JSON keys from inspect_json_envelope.
  • The expected column tuple from schemas.source_columns(dataset).
  • HEADER_OVERRIDES (one explicit mapping for provider_info).
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • A frozen DriftAssessment with has_breaking_drift.
  • List of dicts for schema_drift_log with drift_type of ADDED_COLUMN, MISSING_COLUMN or RENAMED_OR_UNMAPPED_COLUMN.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Build expected_by_key: each expected name is normalised (lower-case, punctuation removed). Two expected names that normalise the same raise ValueError.
  2. For each physical header: strip BOM/whitespace, try the explicit override, then the normalised match.
  3. No match: derive a provisional safe name (provisional_column_name). Empty, non-identifier or reserved name goes to invalid.
  4. A canonical name already used goes to duplicate.
  5. A canonical name not in the expected tuple is recorded as an AddedColumn (kept in the table via mergeSchema).
  6. After the loop, every expected column that was never used is missing.
  7. _drift_records: if anything is missing, added columns are labelled RENAMED_OR_UNMAPPED_COLUMN (a probable rename); otherwise ADDED_COLUMN.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 31–34The matching key. CMS Certification Number (CCN) and cms_certification_number_ccn both become cmscertificationnumberccn, which is how the human-readable bulk CSV header lines up with the snake_case API/Bronze name.
lines 37–50For an unknown new column: lower-case, replace non-identifier characters with _, collapse repeats, prefix source_ if it starts with a digit. Deterministic, so the same new column gets the same Bronze name on every run.
lines 60–76The result object. Breaking means missing, invalid or duplicate. An added column is deliberately not breaking.
lines 91–106Set-up: expected names indexed by normalised key, override map, and empty accumulators.
lines 108–136The classification loop described in the steps. Note override_map is tried first on the exact stripped source name; only then the normalised key.
lines 138–146Anything expected but never matched is missing. The assessment keeps ordered_columns in physical file order so the explicit Spark schema in _csv_dataframe lines up with the CSV positions.
lines 149–178API pages are already snake_case, so this is simpler: exact name match, no renaming. Expected columns come first in ordered, valid new keys are appended.
lines 374–383A new column that appears together with a missing column looks like a rename, so it is labelled RENAMED_OR_UNMAPPED_COLUMN instead of ADDED_COLUMN.
lines 403–416One MISSING_COLUMN row per absent required column. The message states the consequence: the file never reaches Bronze.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • normalize_header_key, provisional_column_name, _expected_by_key (inside drift.py).
  • schemas.HEADER_OVERRIDES, schemas.source_columns.
  • bronze._write_drift → audit.append_typed_records → schema_drift_log.

Called by: bronze.process_manifest_item for every CSV file and API page.

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • Runs before any Spark read: the physical header decides the explicit string schema in _csv_dataframe.
  • If has_breaking_drift, process_manifest_item writes the drift rows first and then raises SchemaDriftError, so the evidence survives even though Bronze is untouched.
  • notebooks/98_prepare_drift_demo.ipynb and 99_demo_idempotency_drift_backfill.ipynb create a copy of a file with an added column to show this path.
  • Added columns persist because _write_batch(..., merge_schema=True) lets Delta evolve the Bronze table.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ACTUAL

I ran the repo's own classify_csv_header locally (pure Python, no Spark) on the header of each local CSV in data/raw/. Result: all four headers classify cleanly (24, 14, 102 and 23 columns; 0 missing, 0 added, no breaking drift), including the single HEADER_OVERRIDES entry that maps the CSV header Total number of nurse staff hours per resident per day on the weekend to the truncated API name total_number_of_nurse_staff_hours_per_resident_per_day_on_t_4a14. Two fixtures: appending a column phase2_demo_added_column to the provider header gives 1 added column, 0 missing, not breaking (logged as ADDED_COLUMN). Removing provider_name and adding provider_nm gives missing=['provider_name'], added provider_nm, breaking (logged as MISSING_COLUMN plus RENAMED_OR_UNMAPPED_COLUMN). The Spark/Delta side of this is not run here.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“Before Spark touches a file, classify_csv_header resolves the physical header against the expected columns. A new column is compatible, so it is logged as ADDED_COLUMN and the Bronze table evolves with mergeSchema. A missing required column is breaking: we log MISSING_COLUMN, raise SchemaDriftError and write nothing, so a silent rename cannot corrupt Silver.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Treat added columns as breaking: every harmless CMS addition would stop the pipeline.
  • Treat missing columns as compatible: renamed columns would become silent NULLs in Bronze and then fail Silver REQUIRED rules, far from the cause.
  • Remove HEADER_OVERRIDES: the weekend nurse-hours column would be classified as added (provisional name) and the expected truncated column as missing, so provider_info would be rejected as breaking drift.
  • Remove ignoreNullFields-style logging: not applicable here; but if _write_drift is skipped, a rejected file leaves no evidence in schema_drift_log.
CRITICAL Trusted work selection & integrity — bronze.select_manifest_items / verify_landing_file / validate_json_envelope · src/carewatch/bronze.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

select_manifest_items decides which landed files Bronze must process by reading source_file_manifest and pipeline_execution_logs, never by scanning folders. verify_landing_file re-hashes the file and compares size and SHA-256 with the manifest. validate_json_envelope checks an API page's _meta block against the manifest.

A landing folder can contain half-written or foreign files. Trusting only manifest rows written after a completed download (SUCCESS or SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED) plus a byte-for-byte integrity check means Bronze only ever ingests exactly what acquisition validated.

2a · Inputs
  • spark, manifest table and log table names.
  • Optional filters: dataset, load_type, acquisition_run_id, source_path, reprocess.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • ManifestSelection(scope_items, process_items): scope is everything not yet validated or without a successful Bronze log; process is the subset still needing a data write (one per (dataset, batch_id)).
  • IntegrityError or EnvelopeValidationError on a mismatch.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Read the manifest, keep only acquisition-successful rows, apply optional filters (source_path must match a manifest row or it raises).
  2. Keep the latest manifest row per (acquisition_run_id, dataset, batch_id, landing_path) using row_number() over load_timestamp desc; order by dataset, run, page_offset.
  3. Build the set of (dataset, batch_id) that already have a SUCCESS Raw-to-Bronze log.
  4. reprocess=false: scope = items not row-count-validated or without a Bronze success log. reprocess=true: scope = everything.
  5. From scope, newest first, keep one item per batch that has no success log (or every item if reprocess).
  6. Later, per item, verify_landing_file and (API pages) validate_json_envelope run before Spark reads anything.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 261–294Returns the set of (dataset, batch_id) whose Raw-to-Bronze log row says SUCCESS (optionally restricted to one Bronze run_id). The log table acts as the checkpoint.
lines 297–315Guards and base filter. _ACQUISITION_STATUSES is ('SUCCESS', 'SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED'): a FAILURE row is never selected.
lines 328–338De-duplicates repeated manifest rows (e.g. a re-used batch) and fixes a stable order so API pages are processed by offset.
lines 345–371Scope vs process. scope also keeps files whose data is already in Bronze but whose row_count_validated flag or watermark was never committed, so reconciliation can repair an interrupted run.
lines 156–172Stops before Spark if the file is missing, its byte count differs, or its SHA-256 differs from the digest recorded at download time.
lines 185–210Reads the small API page in Python and checks the shape: object with _meta dict and results list of objects; collects the union of keys in first-seen order.
lines 224–258dataset_id, load_type and the exact filter string must equal what the manifest says, rows_in_file must equal the real result count, and rows_available must equal the expected total for the run.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • ManifestItem.from_mapping, ManifestSelection, _sha256_file, inspect_json_envelope, _expected_filter.
  • PySpark: Window, row_number, filter, collect; get_dataset for validation.

Called by: Notebook 02_raw_to_bronze (selection) and bronze.process_manifest_item (integrity and envelope checks).

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • Reads what acquire wrote to source_file_manifest.
  • Reads what audited wrote to pipeline_execution_logs.
  • Its scope_items feed reconcile_acquisition_run, which is the only place a watermark advances.
  • Idempotency: a re-run with no new files returns an empty process_items tuple, so nothing is written.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ILLUSTRATIVE

After the scheduled Job's first task downloads one new provider_info snapshot, its manifest row has row_count_validated=false and no Bronze log. select_manifest_items puts it into both scope_items and process_items. After Bronze succeeds and reconciliation sets the flag, the next call returns it in neither. (Illustrative of the code path; the 25 Oct 2026 run's exact manifest rows are not in the repository.)

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“Bronze never lists folders. It asks the manifest what acquisition completed, joins that to the execution log to see what Bronze already finished, and re-hashes each file against the manifest digest before Spark reads it. That is why re-running notebook 02 is safe.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Scan folders instead: partial .partial downloads or hand-copied files could be ingested.
  • Remove the success-log join: every run would rewrite all batches (still idempotent, but slow and logged as work).
  • Remove verify_landing_file: a file edited after download would be ingested silently.
  • Remove scope_items repair logic: a crash between Bronze write and watermark commit would leave a watermark stuck forever.
CRITICAL Per-file Bronze load — bronze.process_manifest_item + _write_batch · src/carewatch/bronze.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

process_manifest_item validates and loads one landed file or API page into a Bronze Delta table and its quarantine table. _write_batch is the idempotent writer that replaces exactly one batch of rows.

This is the heart of Raw-to-Bronze: preserve the source exactly (all columns as strings), add lineage columns, isolate unreadable records, and make a retry overwrite rather than duplicate.

2a · Inputs
  • One ManifestItem.
  • run_id (this Bronze run), catalog and schema names, manifest/drift/quarantine table names.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • Rows appended or replaced in bronze_nh_* (source columns + _dataset_id, _source_file, _source_file_sha256, _batch_id, _load_type, _ingest_date, load_timestamp).
  • Corrupt CSV records in bronze_quarantine with failed_rules = ['CORRUPT_CSV_RECORD'].
  • Drift rows; source_rows written back to the manifest.
  • A BronzeFileResult (rows_read, rows_inserted, rows_quarantined, added_columns).
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. verify_landing_file (size + SHA-256).
  2. JSON page: inspect and validate the envelope, classify_json_keys, read with an explicit schema. CSV: read the header, classify_csv_header, read with an explicit all-string schema in PERMISSIVE mode.
  3. Write drift rows; if breaking drift, raise SchemaDriftError.
  4. CSV: one aggregate gives rows_read and rows_quarantined; split good and bad rows on _corrupt_record. JSON: rows_read = count(); it must equal the inspected row count.
  5. Build the quarantine frame and _write_batch it into bronze_quarantine (keyed by batch_id).
  6. Add lineage columns and _write_batch into the Bronze table (keyed by _batch_id, with mergeSchema).
  7. _update_manifest_source_rows records the parsed row count for reconciliation.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 607–627Entry point. The first real action is verify_landing_file; source_columns(dataset) supplies the expected column list.
lines 629–646Two read paths. API pages cannot have a corrupt CSV field, so has_corrupt_field is False. Bulk and snapshot CSVs use classify_csv_header plus the dataset's override map and can contain corrupt rows. Any other strategy string raises.
lines 455–472The explicit schema is every column a nullable string plus _corrupt_record. PERMISSIVE mode with columnNameOfCorruptRecord puts unparseable lines into that column instead of failing; multiLine plus quote/escape " handle quoted newlines in CMS text fields. No inferSchema anywhere.
lines 476–496API page: an explicit envelope schema (_meta struct + array of all-string records), then explode(results) and flatten.
lines 648–655Drift evidence is persisted before the breaking-drift exception, so a rejected file still leaves a row in schema_drift_log.
lines 657–674CSV: one aggregation counts total and corrupt rows, then the frame is split. API: counts rows only. rows_inserted = rows_read - rows_quarantined.
lines 676–680Cross-check: for an API page, what Spark parsed must equal what Python counted in the envelope.
lines 516–539Quarantine row = dataset, file, SHA-256, batch, the record re-serialised as JSON (ignoreNullFields=false), the raw corrupt text, and the rule label CORRUPT_CSV_RECORD.
lines 499–513Lineage columns appended to the untouched source columns. _batch_id is the key used for idempotent replacement.
lines 542–580Idempotent batch writer. New table: plain append. Existing table with zero rows: delete this batch only. Otherwise overwrite with replaceWhere _batch_id = '<id>', so only that batch's rows are replaced and other batches are untouched; mergeSchema permits accepted added columns.
lines 682–700Quarantine is written first, using the same _write_batch helper keyed on batch_id.
lines 702–718Then the Bronze rows, then the parsed row count goes back to the manifest (every manifest row for the same deterministic batch).
lines 720–730The notebook copies these counts into the audit record.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • verify_landing_file, inspect_json_envelope, validate_json_envelope, classify_json_keys, classify_csv_header, read_csv_header.
  • _csv_dataframe, _json_dataframe, _add_bronze_metadata, _quarantine_dataframe, _write_batch, _write_drift, _update_manifest_source_rows.
  • audit.utc_now, audit.BRONZE_QUARANTINE_SCHEMA, schemas.HEADER_OVERRIDES, schemas.source_columns, config.qualified_name.
  • Delta: DeltaTable.forName(...).delete/update.

Called by: Notebook 02_raw_to_bronze cell 4 inside audited(...), once per item in selection.process_items.

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • Upstream: source_file_manifest rows from notebook 01 and the landed file.
  • Downstream: silver.select_silver_work_items reads bronze_nh_* by _batch_id; Silver reads quarantined/corrupt evidence only through bronze_quarantine counts.
  • Writes source_rows that reconcile_acquisition_run sums and compares with expected_run_rows.
7 · Realistic project-specific example INFERRED

Running the same provider_info batch twice: the first call finds no table (or no rows for that _batch_id) and writes 14,690 rows (the local snapshot has 14,690 data rows). The second call uses replaceWhere _batch_id = '<same id>', replacing those same 14,690 rows, so the table still has 14,690 rows for that batch. The row count is from the local data/raw file; the exact batch id of the deployed run is not in the repository, and the Delta overwrite behaviour is inferred from the code, not executed here.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“Bronze is a faithful copy: every column is a string, with lineage columns added. Each file is one batch. We write a batch with replaceWhere on _batch_id, so a retry replaces that batch instead of appending a duplicate. Unreadable CSV lines are not dropped: they go to bronze_quarantine with a rule label.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Use inferSchema: leading zeros in CCNs would be lost and drift would be invisible.
  • Use plain append: re-running a failed Bronze task duplicates rows, which Silver would then see as exact duplicates or conflicts.
  • Remove _corrupt_record: a malformed line would make the read fail (FAILFAST) or silently disappear.
  • Change _batch_id derivation in acquire._batch_id: replaceWhere would no longer match prior rows and old batches would linger.
CRITICAL Row-count reconciliation & watermark commit — bronze.reconcile_acquisition_run · src/carewatch/bronze.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

After the per-file loop, reconcile_acquisition_run verifies that a whole acquisition run is complete: one authoritative expected row count, every file parsed, parsed total equals expected total, API offsets contiguous, every batch has a Bronze success log. Only then it commits the dataset watermark and sets row_count_validated.

This is the single gate between downloaded and trusted. If it advanced watermarks at acquisition time, a failed Bronze load would permanently skip data. It is the answer to “how do you guarantee no data loss on incremental load?”.

2a · Inputs
  • acquisition_run_id, dataset, this Bronze run_id; manifest, log and watermark table names; optional require_bronze_run_id (used when reprocess).
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • A ReconciliationResult(complete, expected_rows, parsed_rows, watermark_value, detail).
  • On success for datasets with a watermark_col: a monotonic MERGE into ingestion_watermarks.
  • On success: row_count_validated = true on that run's manifest rows.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Load the run's successful manifest rows ordered by page_offset.
  2. Exactly one distinct expected_run_rows, no missing source_rows, and sum(source_rows) == expected_run_rows; else complete=False with a reason.
  3. API runs: offsets must be 0, 500, 1000, … with no gap.
  4. Every batch must have a SUCCESS Raw-to-Bronze log (restricted to this run if require_bronze_run_id).
  5. If the dataset has a watermark column: take the single window_end (API) or the single as_of_date (full load) and call commit_bronze_watermark.
  6. Only after that succeeds, _mark_manifest_run_validated.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 749–773Load the manifest rows for exactly this run and dataset.
lines 780–801Three early exits return complete=False: no single expected count, a file not yet parsed, or parsed ≠ expected. None raises; the notebook turns them into a failing task.
lines 803–815A missing page is detected even if the row total happened to match: pages must be exactly 0, 500, 1000, ….
lines 817–833Every batch must have a Bronze success log: a file whose data was written but whose audit row failed is not trusted.
lines 835–863Watermark value: API runs use the single window_end; full loads use as_of_date. Datasets with no watermark_col (the snapshot-diff feeds) skip this block, so they have no watermark row.
lines 865–868Order matters. Watermark first, validated flag second. A crash between them is safe because the watermark MERGE is monotonic and is simply repeated on the next run.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • _successful_bronze_batch_ids, _mark_manifest_run_validated, ManifestItem.from_mapping.
  • watermarks.commit_bronze_watermark (monotonic MERGE source >= target).
  • config.get_dataset.

Called by: Notebook 02_raw_to_bronze cell 5, once per (acquisition_run_id, dataset) in selection.scope_items.

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • acquire.resolve_window_start and find_*_api_window read the watermark this function commits.
  • Notebook 01's incremental mode fails if no Bronze-committed watermark exists.
  • Notebook 02 raises when any run is not complete, so the Job stops before Silver.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ILLUSTRATIVE

For health_deficiencies the Bronze task of the 25 Oct 2026 run completed in the documented Job run; the Pipeline Health evidence shows Raw-to-Bronze rows for each dataset. The detailed manifest counts of that run are not stored in the repo, so no per-run number is quoted here. What the code guarantees: if the API run expected N rows over pages at offsets 0 and 500 and only the first page reached Bronze, parsed_rows != expected_rows, complete=False, the watermark does not move, and the next run re-selects the missing page.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“A download is not trusted until Bronze proves it. reconcile_acquisition_run checks one authoritative expected count, every file parsed, the sum matches, pages are contiguous and each batch has a Bronze success log. Only then it advances the watermark, and that happens before marking the run validated, so a crash in between just repeats a safe monotonic MERGE.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Advance the watermark in notebook 01: a failed Bronze load would skip those dates forever.
  • Drop the contiguous-offset check: a lost middle page with an unlucky row total would go unnoticed.
  • Swap the order (validated flag before watermark): a crash leaves a validated run whose watermark never moved and is never repaired.
  • Make the MERGE non-monotonic: an old rerun could move the watermark backwards.
CRITICAL Notebook 02 — notebooks/02_raw_to_bronze.ipynb · notebooks/02_raw_to_bronze.ipynb
1 · What it does and why it exists

The orchestration notebook for Raw-to-Bronze. It declares widgets, runs ensure_control_tables, selects work, processes each item inside audited(...), reconciles every acquisition run in scope, displays the results and fails the task if anything is partial.

Notebooks are the Job's tasks. Keeping logic in src/carewatch and only orchestration here makes the code testable and the Databricks Job a thin wrapper.

2a · Inputs
  • Widgets: dataset, load_type, acquisition_run_id, source_path, reprocess, catalog, schema, pipeline_run_id.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • Bronze and quarantine rows, drift rows, audit rows (layer Raw-to-Bronze), watermark commits, displayed result tables.
  • A RuntimeError when files failed or any run stayed partial.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Add src/ to sys.path; import carewatch modules.
  2. Create widgets and collect PARAMETERS.
  3. Set UTC session timezone; map all to None; create a fresh run_id; ensure_control_tables.
  4. select_manifest_items.
  5. Loop selection.process_items: audited(...) around process_manifest_item; copy counts into the record; catch exceptions so one bad file does not block independent files.
  6. Reconcile each (run, dataset) in scope, including repair of earlier interrupted runs.
  7. Display results; raise if any failures or partial runs.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
cell 2, lines 1–22Eight widgets. The Job passes pipeline_run_id={{job.run_id}}; the other widgets keep their defaults for scheduled runs. reprocess is the replay switch (false by default).
cell 3, lines 1–15UTC timezone, widget values normalised, a new run_id, and the additive control-table setup so the notebook is self-healing.
cell 3, lines 23–32The manifest-driven selection described in the previous component.
cell 4, lines 22–34The audited unit of work. The three assignments after the call are what audited later writes to pipeline_execution_logs.
cell 4, lines 51–62audited has already logged the failure; the notebook records it for display and continues so independent files still load.
cell 5, lines 3–20Reconciles every acquisition run in scope, not only runs that had files processed in this execution. That covers a prior crash after Bronze committed but before the watermark did.
cell 6, lines 67–77The failure gate: any file failure or incomplete run raises, so the Job's next task (bronze_to_silver, ALL_SUCCESS) does not run.
5 · Functions / modules it calls

CRITICAL Silver work selection — silver.select_silver_work_items / pending_work_keys / select_bronze_batch · src/carewatch/silver.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

select_silver_work_items returns the Bronze batches that still need Silver processing: acquisition-successful manifest rows, joined to a Raw-to-Bronze success log with rows_inserted > 0, minus batches that already have a terminal Bronze-to-Silver log (SUCCESS or QUARANTINED_PARTIAL). pending_work_keys is the same rule as a pure function. select_bronze_batch reads one batch's rows from Bronze, with optional ingestion-date bounds for backfill.

Silver must be driven by state, not by timestamps or folder listings, so a rerun does exactly the unfinished work. Using the log table as checkpoint is what makes Bronze-to-Silver incremental and restartable.

2a · Inputs
  • spark, manifest and log table names, optional dataset, load_type, acquisition_run_id, batch_ids, reprocess.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • A tuple of SilverWorkItem ordered by manifest load time, dataset, page offset, batch id.
  • A Spark DataFrame of one Bronze batch.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Check both control tables exist and the filters are valid.
  2. Keep manifest rows with status SUCCESS or SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED; apply optional filters.
  3. Count distinct batches per acquisition run (used by the soft-delete gate).
  4. Keep the newest manifest row per (dataset, batch_id).
  5. Inner-join to Raw-to-Bronze logs with status SUCCESS or QUARANTINED_PARTIAL and rows_inserted > 0.
  6. Unless reprocess, left_anti join against Bronze-to-Silver logs with a terminal status.
  7. Order deterministically and collect into SilverWorkItem objects.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 112–128The checkpoint rule in its simplest form: Bronze successes minus Silver terminal attempts. reprocess returns everything Bronze has.
lines 394–418Fail early: both control tables must exist and arguments must be valid.
lines 422–447Manifest filter, per-run file counts, and the newest manifest row per batch. acquisition_file_count later proves a snapshot is a single artifact.
lines 449–457Only batches that Bronze actually wrote (rows_inserted > 0) qualify. A partially quarantined Bronze file still has valid rows, so QUARANTINED_PARTIAL is accepted too.
lines 459–469The Silver checkpoint: drop any batch that already has a terminal Bronze-to-Silver log. A batch whose last attempt was FAILURE is not terminal, so it is retried.
lines 471–482Deterministic order so reruns behave identically.
lines 485–502Reads exactly one batch by _batch_id; ingest_from/ingest_to narrow it on _ingest_date for date-bounded backfills (the notebook then refuses to checkpoint a partial batch).
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • get_dataset, SilverWorkItem.from_mapping, SILVER_TERMINAL_STATUSES, ACQUISITION_SUCCESS_STATUSES.
  • PySpark: Window, row_number, joins (inner, left_anti).

Called by: Notebook 03_bronze_to_silver cell 3 (work items) and cell 4 (select_bronze_batch).

  • Reads Raw-to-Bronze logs written by notebook 02 via audited.
  • Reads manifest rows written by notebook 01.
  • Writes nothing; the notebook writes the Bronze-to-Silver log that makes a batch ‘complete’.
  • work_items empty ⇒ notebook prints “No successful Bronze batches require Silver processing.” and exits cleanly (this is the idempotent re-run).

After a Bronze task commits one health_deficiencies API page, that batch id is in the Raw-to-Bronze log with rows_inserted > 0 and not in the Bronze-to-Silver log, so it is selected. After Silver finishes it writes a SUCCESS or QUARANTINED_PARTIAL row; the same call returns it no more. A batch that failed Silver has only a FAILURE log, so it is selected again.

Say this

“Silver is driven by logs, not folders. A batch is pending if Bronze succeeded and wrote rows but there is no terminal Silver log. SUCCESS and QUARANTINED_PARTIAL are terminal; FAILURE is not, so failures retry automatically.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Treat only SUCCESS as terminal: any batch with even one quarantined row would be reprocessed on every run.
  • Drop the rows_inserted > 0 check: batches with no Bronze rows would hit the “no rows in Bronze” error.
  • Remove the left_anti join: all batches reprocess each run (still idempotent via MERGE, but wasted compute and noisy logs).
CRITICAL Silver transformation — silver.transform_bronze_batch · src/carewatch/silver.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

One function turns one Bronze batch (all strings) into (a) an accepted DataFrame matching the explicit Silver schema and (b) a quarantine DataFrame of rejected rows, plus the counts. It trims and null-normalises text, type-casts safely, evaluates every validation rule, computes the entity key and row hash, hashes the address with a secret salt, removes exact duplicates and quarantines conflicting keys.

This is where raw CMS text becomes trustworthy, typed, privacy-safe data. Rows are never silently dropped: every rejected input row ends up in silver_quarantine with the exact rule names that failed.

2a · Inputs
  • A Bronze batch DataFrame, the dataset name, address_secret_scope and address_secret_key (names only, never the salt).
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • SilverTransformResult: accepted, quarantine, rows_read, rows_accepted, rows_rejected, invalid_input_rows, conflicting_input_rows, unique_quarantine_records, exact_valid_duplicates_collapsed, max_source_processing_date.
  • SilverSchemaError if Bronze lacks required columns.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Guard: Bronze must contain every source column plus _source_file, _source_file_sha256, _batch_id, _ingest_date.
  2. Snapshot the original raw record as JSON (_raw_record_original), trim all strings and turn empty strings into NULL.
  3. Build one expression per Silver business column: address hash, derived severity_group, upper-casing, Y/N to boolean, or try_cast to the target type.
  4. Append lineage and _raw__<col> helpers; compute _failed_rules by evaluating all rule expressions.
  5. Compute the entity key (only when non-null key fields are present) and row_hash.
  6. Split: invalid (any failed rule) and valid. Within valid, keys with more than one distinct row_hash are conflicts.
  7. accepted = valid, non-conflicting, dropDuplicates([key, row_hash]); quarantine = invalid ∪ conflicting, de-duplicated.
  8. Count everything and verify conservation with calculate_transform_metrics.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 702–736Contract guard: extra Bronze columns are tolerated, but any required column missing raises SilverSchemaError.
lines 738–754Keeps the untouched original as JSON (for quarantine), then trims all source columns and converts '' to NULL, which is the Silver string-normalisation rule.
lines 762–776Privacy. The Silver column is sha2(upper(provider_address) + secret(scope,key), 256); NULL address stays NULL. Clear-text address is not copied to Silver.
lines 777–787Business rule used by the dashboard: scope/severity letters A-C, D-F, G-I, J-L. G-L are the ‘serious’ groups used in the Gold measures.
lines 788–800Every other column: optional upper-casing (CCN, state, tag prefix, severity), strict Y/N to boolean, otherwise try_cast to the target type. try_cast returns NULL on bad data instead of throwing, which the rule engine then reports.
lines 802–813Assembles the typed frame plus source_processing_date (the CMS processing_date as a date), _raw__<col> helper columns (to detect ‘had text but cast to NULL’) and lineage names.
lines 814–819Evaluates every rule and keeps only the names that fired, as an array column _failed_rules.
lines 821–835Entity key = SHA-256 of ordered JSON of the business-key columns (only when the non-nullable key parts are present); row_hash = SHA-256 of all retained business columns. Both are described in the hashing component.
lines 837–853Split. A key with two different row hashes inside the same valid slice is a conflict: it is quarantined rather than silently choosing a row. Identical duplicates (same key and same hash) collapse to one.
lines 855–879Quarantine row: dataset, source batch/file/SHA-256, candidate entity key, the original raw record JSON, sorted failed rule names, load time. dropDuplicates makes the quarantine itself deterministic.
lines 881–898Counts, then calculate_transform_metrics enforces rows_read = invalid + conflicting + valid_nonconflicting; if not, it raises.
lines 176–209The conservation check: negative counts raise, categories must sum to rows_read, accepted can never exceed valid non-conflicting.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • silver_validation_spec, silver_business_columns, SILVER_SCHEMAS, SILVER_ENTITY_KEYS, SILVER_BUSINESS_KEYS, SOURCE_COLUMNS (from schemas.py).
  • databricks_secret_expression, sha256_json_columns, _try_cast, _validation_rule_expressions, missing_required_columns, calculate_transform_metrics.

Called by: Notebook 03_bronze_to_silver cell 4, inside audited(...), once per Bronze batch.

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • Input: a Bronze batch from select_bronze_batch.
  • Output accepted goes to merge_silver_batch; quarantine goes to append_quarantine_idempotently.
  • rows_read and rows_rejected become the audit record, which turns a run into QUARANTINED_PARTIAL when rejected rows exist.
  • max_source_processing_date bounds soft deletion.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ACTUAL

For deficiencies the local CMS file has 418,947 rows. Mirroring the declarative rules in pure Python over data/raw/r5ix-sfxw.csv gives exactly one failing rule, CONDITIONAL:correction_date_required, on 36 rows (status ‘Deficient, Provider has date of correction’ but an empty correction date); 0 rows fail any regex/domain/cast rule; all 418,947 business keys are distinct, so 0 conflicts. Expected Silver outcome: 418,947 read, 36 quarantined, 418,911 accepted. That matches the Gold fact_deficiency row count (418,911) and the saved Pipeline Health evidence (rows_read=418,947, rows_quarantined=36). The same mirror finds 0 failing rows in penalties (15,419), MDS (249,730) and provider information (14,690). The mirror is a hand transcription of the rules, not the Spark code, so exact Spark equivalence is INFERRED.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“transform_bronze_batch is the Silver brain. It trims and null-normalises, safe-casts, evaluates all validation rules into an array of failed rule names, hashes keys, and splits the batch. Bad rows go to silver_quarantine with the rule names, conflicting keys are quarantined rather than guessed, exact duplicates collapse, and a conservation check makes sure no row is lost: read = rejected + accepted + collapsed.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Use cast instead of try_cast: one bad value fails the whole batch instead of quarantining one row.
  • Drop the conflict logic: two different rows for one key would both go to MERGE and the winner would be arbitrary.
  • Put the clear-text address in Silver: the privacy requirement fails.
  • Change business_columns or their order: every row_hash changes and the next run rewrites every Silver row (a useful way to demonstrate hash-based change detection, but harmful in production).
CRITICAL Declarative validation rules — schemas.SILVER_VALIDATION_SPECS + silver._validation_rule_expressions · src/carewatch/schemas.py + src/carewatch/silver.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

Rules are data in schemas.py (SilverValidationSpec per dataset) and are turned into Spark boolean expressions by _validation_rule_expressions. Each rule yields a label such as REGEX:state, DOMAIN:scope_severity_code, RANGE:overall_rating, SAFE_CAST:survey_date->survey_date, NON_NEGATIVE:fine_amount or CONDITIONAL:fine_subtype.

Separating what is valid from how it is evaluated keeps rules readable, auditable and consistent across four datasets, and lets the quarantine table report exactly which rule failed.

2a · Inputs
  • Dataset name and the typed DataFrame (cast columns plus _raw__<col> helpers).
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • A list of (condition, rule_name) pairs; transform_bronze_batch collects the names of conditions that are true.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Required fields: NULL ⇒ REQUIRED:<field>.
  2. Safe-cast fields: raw text present but cast result NULL ⇒ SAFE_CAST:<source>-><target>.
  3. Boolean Y/N fields: raw present but result NULL ⇒ DOMAIN_YN:<field>.
  4. Regex rules, allowed-value rules, numeric ranges (RANGE), non-negatives (NON_NEGATIVE).
  5. Dataset-specific CONDITIONAL rules for deficiencies and penalties.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 725–753The shape of a rule set: required fields, safe-cast fields, upper-cased fields, Y/N fields, regex, allowed values, numeric ranges, non-negative fields and descriptive conditional rules. frozen=True so rules cannot change at runtime.
lines 844–880The deficiency rules: CCN ^[0-9A-Z]{6}$, state ^[A-Z]{2}$, ZIP ^[0-9]{5}$, tag ^[0-9]{4}$, severity letter A-L, inspection cycle 1/2/3, five Y/N flags, six business-key fields required.
lines 597–604Builds the rule list for a dataset from its spec.
lines 606–617REQUIRED and SAFE_CAST. The _raw__ helper columns let the code tell ‘source was empty’ (allowed NULL) from ‘source had text that failed to cast’ (a rule failure).
lines 619–626Y/N flags: any other non-empty text is a DOMAIN_YN failure.
lines 628–644Regex and allowed-value checks only fire when the value is not NULL (NULL is handled by REQUIRED).
lines 646–662Range and non-negative checks; used e.g. for star ratings 1–5, latitude/longitude, MDS scores 0–100.
lines 664–671The cross-field rule: if the status says a correction date exists, correction_date must not be NULL. This is the rule behind the 36 quarantined deficiency rows.
lines 672–699Penalties are a union of two subtypes. A Fine needs fine_id and fine_amount and no payment-denial fields; a Payment Denial needs start date and length and no fine fields.
5 · Functions / modules it calls

Called by: transform_bronze_batch.
