CRITICAL Keys, row hash & address hashing — sha256_json_columns, canonical_json_sha256, databricks_secret_expression · src/carewatch/silver.py + src/carewatch/schemas.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

Three small functions underpin Silver's identity and privacy design. sha256_json_columns builds the Spark expression sha2(to_json(struct(cols), ignoreNullFields=false), 256) used for entity keys (hash of business-key columns) and row hashes (hash of all business columns). canonical_json_sha256 is a pure-Python reference of the same contract. databricks_secret_expression builds the SQL secret(scope, key) call used as the address-hash salt.

A deterministic key lets MERGE match the same real-world entity across loads. A row hash lets MERGE detect change by comparing one string. Keeping NULLs explicit prevents {a:null,b:1} and {b:1} colliding. The salt is resolved inside Spark and never enters Python or the repository.

2a · Inputs
  • Ordered list of column names.
  • Secret scope and key names (not the secret value).
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • A Spark column expression (64-hex SHA-256), or a hex string from the pure helper.
  • A Spark expression secret('scope','key').
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Order matters: columns are taken in a fixed tuple order (SILVER_BUSINESS_KEYS[dataset] / silver_business_columns(dataset)).
  2. to_json with ignoreNullFields=false serialises NULLs explicitly.
  3. sha2(..., 256) hashes the JSON text.
  4. Address: sha2(concat(upper(provider_address), secret(scope,key)), 256); Databricks resolves the secret in the engine.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 139–148Pure reference: ordered dict → compact JSON (no spaces, ensure_ascii=False) → SHA-256. It exists so the contract can be tested without Spark.
lines 543–552The production expression: to_json(struct(...), {ignoreNullFields:false}) then sha2(…, 256). Each column is re-aliased to its own name so the JSON keys are the column names, in order.
lines 567–583Only the non-secret names are placed in the SQL expression. The value is resolved by Databricks inside Spark. Empty scope/key raises.
lines 697–721The written contract: three fields are dropped entirely (telephone_number, provider_address, location); keys and row hashes use ordered null-preserving JSON; the address hash uses a Databricks-secret salt; exact duplicates collapse; conflicting keys do not.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • PySpark to_json, struct, sha2, expr.
  • Python hashlib, json.

Called by: transform_bronze_batch (entity key, row hash, address hash).

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • facility_key / deficiency_key / penalty_key / mds_key are the MERGE join keys in merge_silver_batch.
  • Gold reuses deficiency_key, penalty_key and mds_key as the fact primary keys and recomputes facility_key with the same sha256_json_columns over the CCN, so one CCN has the same key in Silver and Gold.
  • gold.validate_deployed_gold bans provider_address_hash (and the other privacy columns) from every Gold table, so the hash stays in Silver.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ACTUAL

For CCN 145239 the reference helper gives: facility_key payload {"cms_certification_number_ccn":"145239"} → 13e87de1b524202804c1806456506ba33c1366e867e01b9755790650477ce0e2. The deficiency payload {"cms_certification_number_ccn":"145239","survey_date":"2026-06-17","survey_type":"Health","deficiency_prefix":"F","deficiency_tag_number":"0689","inspection_cycle":1} → deficiency_key 17c9edd5b8896e184bed1e7a841288c7296ddd285b711e478bb36b0932f2c4e4. Computed with silver.canonical_json_sha256 on the local CSV values; that the Spark to_json output is byte-identical is INFERRED (not executed). The address hash cannot be reproduced because the salt lives only in Databricks Secrets.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“Identity and change detection use SHA-256 over ordered JSON with explicit nulls. The business key hash is the MERGE key; the row hash tells MERGE whether anything changed. The address is hashed with a salt that lives only in Databricks Secrets and is resolved inside Spark, so it never touches Python code, the repo or the Silver table.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Change column order or omit ignoreNullFields=false: all hashes change, so MERGE sees every row as changed or as new.
  • Put the salt in code: it would be committed to git (the privacy design fails).
  • Remove the salt: addresses could be re-identified by dictionary attack on a plain SHA-256.
  • Treat key columns case-insensitively: CCN is upper-cased before hashing for exactly this reason; removing that would create duplicate entities.
CRITICAL Silver upsert — merge_silver_batch, should_apply_change, append_quarantine_idempotently · src/carewatch/silver.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

merge_silver_batch upserts accepted rows into the Silver Delta table by entity key. A matching key is updated only when the content changed and the source row is not older than the stored one; a new key is inserted. append_quarantine_idempotently appends only quarantine rows not already present.

Silver must be rerunnable. Hash-based change detection makes a repeated batch a no-op, and the processing-date guard prevents a late-arriving old file from overwriting newer data. This is SCD Type 1 (current-state) behaviour as the proposal states.

2a · Inputs
  • The accepted DataFrame, Silver table name and entity key column; the quarantine DataFrame and quarantine table.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • MergeMetrics(rows_inserted, rows_updated) taken from Delta's operationMetrics.
  • The number of new quarantine rows written.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Empty source ⇒ return zero metrics.
  2. Build update_map / insert_map from the source columns.
  3. MERGE on target.<key> = source.<key>.
  4. WHEN MATCHED AND (row_hash differs OR target is deleted) AND source_processing_date IS NOT NULL AND (target date IS NULL OR source date >= target date) ⇒ update all columns.
  5. WHEN NOT MATCHED ⇒ insert.
  6. Read the inserted/updated counts from the latest Delta history entry.
  7. Quarantine: null-safe left_anti join on seven identity columns, then append only the new rows.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 256–275The pure decision, documented as ‘conservative’: unchanged ⇒ no write; a changed row without a source processing date cannot prove it is newer, so it is not allowed to overwrite; otherwise only when the source is at least as new.
lines 961–995The same rule as a Delta MERGE condition. Re-running the same batch finds row_hash equal everywhere, so zero rows are updated and none inserted. is_deleted = true also qualifies so that a soft-deleted entity that reappears is revived.
lines 915–953A retry would otherwise duplicate quarantine rows. The join uses eqNullSafe because candidate_entity_key can be NULL for rows that lacked a key.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • DeltaTable.forName(...).alias(...).merge(...).whenMatchedUpdate(...).whenNotMatchedInsert(...).execute().
  • _latest_delta_metrics (reads history(1) operationMetrics).

Called by: Notebook 03_bronze_to_silver cell 4.

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • Writes silver_facility, silver_deficiency, silver_penalty, silver_mds_quality.
  • Gold builds every output from the full current Silver state, so a Silver update flows through at the next Gold run.
  • The metrics go into rows_inserted / rows_updated of the Bronze-to-Silver log row.
7 · Realistic project-specific example INFERRED

Idempotency demo (code path): run Bronze-to-Silver for a batch, note rows_inserted; run again. The second run is not even selected (terminal log exists). With reprocess=true it is selected; every row_hash matches, so rows_inserted=0 and rows_updated=0. Recorded evidence of the same no-op behaviour on the Gold side: the repository's README/evidence for the 25 Oct 2026 scheduled run reports zero Gold mutations.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“Silver is an SCD Type 1 current-state table. MERGE on the entity key; update only when the row hash changed and the incoming processing date is not older than the stored one. That makes reruns no-ops and stops stale backfills from overwriting newer data.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Remove the hash condition: every run rewrites every row (slow, noisy history).
  • Remove the date guard: replaying an old batch would roll current data back.
  • Use append instead of MERGE: reruns create duplicates and Gold row counts double.
  • Add whenNotMatchedBySource delete here: a partial batch would delete everything else (the reason deletes are a separate, gated step).
IMPORTANT Gated soft deletes — evaluate_soft_delete, is_latest_validated_snapshot, soft_delete_missing_rows · src/carewatch/silver.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

Disabled by default. When explicitly enabled and every safety gate passes, rows missing from the newest complete snapshot are marked is_deleted = true (not physically removed).

A snapshot-style feed (provider information) can legitimately drop a facility. But deleting based on an incomplete batch would wipe valid data, so deletion is allowed only if the snapshot is provably complete, latest and clean.

2a · Inputs
  • A SilverWorkItem, the allow_soft_deletes widget, whether the run is a subset/reprocess, the batch's rejected count, the latest-snapshot check and the batch's max processing date.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • SoftDeleteDecision(allowed, reasons).
  • If allowed: number of rows soft-deleted (rows_deleted).
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Collect every reason deletion is not allowed: not enabled, subset/backfill/reprocess, API window, manifest not successful, row-count validation incomplete, not exactly one artifact, counts unavailable/mismatched/zero, quarantined rows present, not the newest validated snapshot, no processing-date bound.
  2. Allowed only if the reason list is empty.
  3. soft_delete_missing_rows runs whenNotMatchedBySourceUpdate for rows with is_deleted = false and source_processing_date <= snapshot max date, setting is_deleted = true and a new load_timestamp.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 278–314Twelve possible ‘reasons’ (some gates have several branches); all that apply are listed (useful in the notebook's displayed soft_delete_reasons).
lines 505–540Among validated, Bronze-successful snapshots of this dataset, ordered by as_of_date then load_timestamp, this batch must be the newest.
lines 998–1025The only delete in Silver. It is a soft delete via whenNotMatchedBySourceUpdate, bounded by processing date so rows newer than the snapshot are untouched. Gold later sets is_currently_listed = false on dim_facility for a CCN whose Silver facility row is soft-deleted, and the Gold aggregate ignores facts whose is_deleted is true.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • SoftDeleteDecision, Delta whenNotMatchedBySourceUpdate, history(1).

Called by: Notebook 03_bronze_to_silver cell 4.

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • allow_soft_deletes widget defaults to false, and deployment/carewatch_daily_incremental.job.json sets "allow_soft_deletes": "false" explicitly for the bronze_to_silver task.
  • Deleted rows reappear (revived) through the MERGE condition target.is_deleted = true.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ILLUSTRATIVE

Illustrative: if a new validated provider_info snapshot omitted CCN 145239, and the run enabled soft deletes with no quarantined rows, that facility's Silver row would get is_deleted = true. Isolated tests recorded in the evidence folder show rows_deleted=2 for a controlled test schema.

Say this

“Deletes are opt-in and heavily gated: complete, validated, newest snapshot, one file, counts reconcile, nothing quarantined. They are soft, so history is not lost and a returning facility is revived by the MERGE.”

CRITICAL Notebook 03 — notebooks/03_bronze_to_silver.ipynb · notebooks/03_bronze_to_silver.ipynb
1 · What it does and why it exists

Orchestrates Bronze-to-Silver: validates that Silver and quarantine tables match their locked schemas, requires the secret scope/key names, selects work, and for each batch runs transform → quarantine append → MERGE → optional soft delete, all inside audited(...).

Everything is wrapped so that one failing batch is logged and left pending, while independent batches still commit. The notebook refuses to run against a non-current quarantine schema or a missing secret reference.

2a · Inputs
  • Widgets: dataset, load_type, acquisition_run_id, batch_ids, ingest_from, ingest_to, reprocess, allow_soft_deletes, address_secret_scope, address_secret_key, catalog, schema, pipeline_run_id.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • Silver rows, quarantine rows, Bronze-to-Silver audit rows, displayed per-batch results and failures.
  • RuntimeError if any batch failed.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Parse and validate widgets (ISO dates, bool flags, ingest_from <= ingest_to).
  2. Require the quarantine table to be in the current eight-column state and every Silver table to match its exact schema; require Bronze tables to exist.
  3. Require secret scope and key names (the value is never fetched into Python).
  4. select_silver_work_items; compute subset_or_reprocess.
  5. Per batch inside audited: read Bronze; for date-filtered runs refuse to checkpoint a partial batch; transform; append quarantine; MERGE; evaluate and maybe apply soft delete.
  6. Collect results/failures, display, and raise if any failure.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
cell 2, lines 1–32Thirteen widgets. The Job supplies address_secret_scope=carewatch-address-hashing, address_secret_key=salt-v1 (names only) and the shared pipeline_run_id.
cell 3, lines 25–32Schema gate: Silver will not run against a legacy quarantine table.
cell 3, lines 34–47Every Silver table must match its explicit schema exactly; Bronze must exist; the secret reference must be provided.
cell 3, lines 53–68Work selection. subset_or_reprocess becomes true for any narrowing parameter, which blocks soft deletes.
cell 4, lines 30–69Reads the batch; a successful Bronze batch with zero rows is an error; with ingestion-date bounds the notebook checks the batch is processed whole, otherwise it suppresses the audit log (no terminal checkpoint) or raises.
cell 4, lines 71–90The core pipeline: transform, write quarantine idempotently, MERGE, and copy counts into the audit record.
cell 4, lines 92–111Soft-delete decision; only applied when every gate passes.
cell 4, lines 134–141Failure isolation: record the failure and continue; the batch has only a FAILURE log, so it is retried next run.
cell 5, lines 12–20End gate: raise if anything failed, so the Gold task does not run.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • carewatch.silver (select_silver_work_items, select_bronze_batch, transform_bronze_batch, append_quarantine_idempotently, merge_silver_batch, evaluate_soft_delete, is_latest_validated_snapshot, soft_delete_missing_rows, table_names).
  • carewatch.audit.audited, suppress_audit_log, require_exact_table_schema, silver_quarantine_schema_state; carewatch.schemas.SILVER_SCHEMAS, SILVER_ENTITY_KEYS.

Called by: Job task bronze_to_silver (depends on raw_to_bronze).

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • Reads Bronze tables and control tables.
  • Writes Silver, silver_quarantine, and pipeline_execution_logs.
  • A failure stops 04_silver_to_gold.
7 · Realistic project-specific example INFERRED

Manual demo parameters: dataset=health_deficiencies, reprocess=false, secret scope carewatch-address-hashing, key salt-v1. Expected: if nothing pending it prints “No successful Bronze batches require Silver processing.”; if a batch is pending the displayed result has rows_read, rows_accepted, input_rows_rejected, quarantine_records_written.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“Notebook 03 checks the contracts first (exact schemas, secret reference), then for each pending batch runs transform, quarantine, MERGE and optional soft delete in an audited block. Failures are logged and retried, successes are never reprocessed.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Remove the schema checks: a drifted Silver table would be MERGEd into silently.
  • Remove the partial-batch guard: a date-filtered backfill could mark a batch ‘done’ when only part of it was processed.
  • Remove the final raise: Gold would run on incomplete Silver.

E4 · Silver-to-Gold, contract and setup/demo notebooks

CRITICAL Gold contract & dimensions — GOLD_PRIMARY_KEYS / GOLD_FOREIGN_KEYS, build_dim_facility, build_dim_deficiency, build_dim_measure, add_mds_period_end · src/carewatch/gold.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

The Gold layer is a star schema. GOLD_PRIMARY_KEYS and GOLD_FOREIGN_KEYS declare every key and relationship; the build_dim_* functions create the five dimensions from the complete current Silver state; add_mds_period_end validates the MDS period label and derives the quarter-end date used to join dim_date.

Power BI needs conformed dimensions and facts at a stated grain. Declaring keys and foreign keys as data lets the same contract drive both the build and the validation (validate_staged_outputs, validate_deployed_gold).

2a · Inputs
  • Silver DataFrames: facility, deficiency, penalty and MDS (read once and cached by stage_gold_outputs).
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • dim_facility (grain: one row per CCN seen in any dataset), dim_date (one row per calendar day), dim_geography (one row per state plus an unknown member), dim_deficiency (one row per prefix + tag + category), dim_measure (one row per measure code + resident type).
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. dim_facility: union all four CCN sets, hash the CCN into facility_key, left-join profile attributes from Silver facility, set is_currently_listed = exists in Silver facility and not soft-deleted.
  2. dim_date: generate every calendar day between the earliest month start and latest event date (survey, penalty, MDS period end).
  3. dim_geography: distinct trimmed state codes from all four sources + __UNKNOWN__.
  4. dim_deficiency: distinct prefix/tag/category; key = hash of those three.
  5. dim_measure: latest description per measure code + resident type; raises if the latest descriptions conflict.
  6. Every output goes through _with_business_hash, adding business_hash and load_timestamp.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 180–190Primary keys. Note the aggregate has a composite key (state_key, month_date_key).
lines 204–226Foreign keys as (fact column, dimension, dimension column) triples. Every fact has facility_key, a date key and state_key; deficiencies add deficiency_type_key; MDS adds measure_key. These same triples are checked before and after deployment.
lines 321–361Facilities are the union of CCNs from all four Silver tables, so a CCN that appears only in an event table still gets a dimension row (profile columns would be NULL and is_currently_listed false). facility_key uses the same hash function as Silver. Only a handful of profile attributes are carried; no address, phone or location.
lines 424–434A type dimension for citations (prefix, tag number, category). Null-safe join keys are used later in the fact build.
lines 437–468One row per MDS measure and resident type. If the most recent Silver rows disagree on the description, the build fails instead of choosing one.
lines 292–3182025Q2-2026Q1 → regex-extract start/end year and quarter, require a valid, ordered label, and compute the last day of the end quarter (2026-03-31). Invalid labels yield NULL and make stage_gold_outputs raise.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • _sha256_json_columns → silver.sha256_json_columns, _with_business_hash, _date_key.
  • PySpark joins, unionByName, Window, dense_rank, make_date, last_day.

Called by: gold.stage_gold_outputs.

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • Dimensions are built before facts because the facts join to them to resolve surrogate keys.
  • validate_staged_outputs checks the foreign keys declared here.
  • Power BI relationships are one-to-many dimension → fact, mirroring these FKs.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ACTUAL

The local provider CSV has 14,690 distinct CCNs and none of the deficiency, penalty or MDS files contains a CCN absent from it. So dim_facility has 14,690 rows, which is exactly the dim_facility row count in the Architectural Report evidence (14,690). dim_measure has 17 rows (the local MDS file has 17 distinct measure code + resident type pairs, matching the report). For CCN 145239 (GOLDWATER CARE PEORIA HEIGHTS, IL) the key is 13e87de1b524202804c1806456506ba33c1366e867e01b9755790650477ce0e2.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“Gold is a star schema built from the full current Silver state. Facility is the union of every CCN seen anywhere, date is a generated calendar, geography has an unknown member so no fact can be orphaned, and every key and foreign key is declared once in GOLD_PRIMARY_KEYS / GOLD_FOREIGN_KEYS and enforced by validation.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Build dim_facility from only Silver facility: facts for CCNs missing from the provider file would have a NULL facility_key and fail the FK check.
  • Remove the unknown geography member: deficiencies with a missing state could not resolve state_key.
  • Change facility_key hashing: it would no longer equal the Silver key; Power BI relationships still work (they use Gold keys) but cross-layer joins break.
CRITICAL Gold facts & aggregate — build_fact_deficiency, build_agg_state_monthly_compliance, _with_business_hash · src/carewatch/gold.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

build_fact_deficiency (and its siblings build_fact_penalty, build_fact_mds_quality) resolve surrogate keys by joining Silver rows to the dimensions and add additive measures. build_agg_state_monthly_compliance sums deficiencies and penalties by state and month. _with_business_hash adds a hash over the business columns for change detection.

Facts hold the measurable events; the aggregate pre-computes the state/month trend used on the dashboard. The business_hash lets the Gold MERGE touch only changed rows.

2a · Inputs
  • Silver deficiency (and penalty/MDS) frames and the freshly built dimensions.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • fact_deficiency (grain: one deficiency citation = one survey date, type, tag, cycle, facility), fact_penalty (one fine or payment denial), fact_mds_quality (one facility × measure × period), agg_state_monthly_compliance (one state × month).
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Left-join to dim_facility on CCN to get facility_key.
  2. Compute survey_date_key (yyyyMMdd int) and join dim_date; resolve state_key from the event's own state (falling back to __UNKNOWN__); resolve deficiency_type_key through a null-safe join on prefix, tag and category.
  3. Select only analytic columns: keys, dates, severity, correction fields, citation_count = 1, serious_citation_count (1 when severity_group is G-I or J-L), is_deleted, lineage ids.
  4. Aggregate: group non-deleted deficiencies and penalties by state and month start; full-outer join them; replace missing values with 0; month key yyyyMMdd.
  5. _with_business_hash computes business_hash from GOLD_BUSINESS_COLUMNS (everything except the PK, the hash and load_timestamp).
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 279–289Adds business_hash and load_timestamp, then selects columns in the exact contract order (validation compares column lists).
lines 471–531The central fact. deficiency_key is carried over from Silver. The count columns are additive: citation_count is always 1, serious_citation_count is 1 for severity groups G-I and J-L. No address, phone, raw record or file path is carried.
lines 646–703Pre-aggregate: both sides exclude is_deleted rows; a full outer join keeps months that have only citations or only penalties; coalesce(..., 0) avoids NULL totals.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • _date_key, _sha256_json_columns, PySpark joins (left, eqNullSafe), groupBy, agg.

Called by: gold.stage_gold_outputs.

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • validate_staged_outputs checks that the fact row counts equal the Silver row counts and that the aggregate totals equal the sums of the non-deleted facts.
  • Power BI measures (not accessible in the .pbix) sum serious_citation_count, fine_amount and use the aggregate for trends.
  • The 36 quarantined deficiency rows never reach Silver, so they are not in fact_deficiency.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ACTUAL

CCN 145239's deficiency of 2026-06-17, tag F0689, severity G, cycle 1 becomes one fact_deficiency row with citation_count=1, serious_citation_count=1, survey_date_key=20260617, deficiency_key=17c9edd5…32c4e4 and state_key='IL'. Locally the CCN has 117 deficiency rows, 16 of them severity G or above, 11 within the dashboard's 12-month window (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30), which equals the value shown on the saved Power BI screenshot. Gold row counts from the report: fact_deficiency 418,911 (= 418,947 local rows − 36 quarantined), fact_penalty 15,419, fact_mds_quality 249,730, aggregate 3,112.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“Facts are at the lowest grain: one row per citation, per penalty, per facility-measure-period. Measures are additive flags, so any BI tool can sum them. The state-month aggregate is pre-computed, and validation proves the aggregate equals the sum of the detail rows.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Include is_deleted rows in the aggregate: totals would exceed the detail facts and reconciliation raises.
  • Change the grain (e.g. drop inspection_cycle from Silver keys): the fact would then contain duplicates; validate_staged_outputs raises on duplicate PKs.
  • Change serious_citation_count severity rule: every dashboard KPI for serious citations changes.
CRITICAL Gold staging & pre-merge validation — stage_gold_outputs / validate_staged_outputs · src/carewatch/gold.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

stage_gold_outputs reads the four Silver tables once, runs input contract checks, then builds all nine Gold outputs in dependency order (all cached, nothing written). validate_staged_outputs then proves they are internally consistent before any target table is touched.

Gold has nine tables and Delta cannot commit them atomically. Building and validating everything before the first MERGE means a data problem fails the task with Gold untouched.

2a · Inputs
  • spark, catalog and schema names.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • (outputs, silver_counts): a dict of nine cached DataFrames and the four Silver row counts.
  • GoldValidationError on any contract breach.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Cache the four Silver tables and count them.
  2. Each must have no NULL key or CCN and no duplicate key.
  3. add_mds_period_end; any invalid or backwards period raises.
  4. Build dimensions, then facts, then the aggregate.
  5. Validate: exact column list per table; no NULL or duplicate PK; no NULL business_hash.
  6. Fact row counts must equal Silver row counts (fact_deficiency = silver_deficiency, etc.).
  7. Every foreign key must resolve (a left_anti join must be empty).
  8. The aggregate must reconcile to the non-deleted facts for six totals.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 706–716Read Silver once, cache it, count it.
lines 717–736Input contract: no NULL entity key, no NULL CCN, no duplicate key in any Silver table.
lines 737–742An invalid MDS period label stops Gold.
lines 744–779Dependency order: facility, date, geography, deficiency, measure → facts → aggregate. Everything is cached, nothing is written yet.
lines 788–807Structural checks on every output: column list equals the contract, no NULL/duplicate primary key, no NULL hash.
lines 809–819Conservation: one fact row per Silver row. This is why fact_deficiency has 418,911 rows, the number of Silver rows after 36 were quarantined.
lines 821–837Referential integrity: for each declared FK a left_anti join must find no orphan.
lines 839–854Reconciliation: citation, serious-citation, penalty, fine, payment-denial counts and fine total in the aggregate must equal the sums of the non-deleted detail facts.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • build_dim_*, build_fact_*, build_agg_state_monthly_compliance, add_mds_period_end, _duplicate_count.
  • GOLD_SCHEMAS, GOLD_PRIMARY_KEYS, GOLD_FOREIGN_KEYS.

Called by: gold.refresh_gold.

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • Reads silver_* tables written by notebook 03.
  • A GoldValidationError makes 04_silver_to_gold fail inside audited, which logs FAILURE and stops the Job.
  • Because nothing has been merged yet, a failure here leaves Gold exactly as it was.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ACTUAL

The local row counts fit the checks: Silver deficiency would be 418,947 − 36 = 418,911, and the report's Gold fact_deficiency is 418,911. Total rows_read for the 25 Oct 2026 Gold audit row is 698,750 = 14,690 + 418,911 + 15,419 + 249,730 (sum of the four Silver counts as documented in the Architectural Report).

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“Gold never merges unvalidated data. It builds all nine tables in memory, then proves column contracts, primary keys, row-count conservation against Silver, every foreign key, and aggregate-versus-detail totals. Only then does it MERGE.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Skip validation: an orphan key would silently make a fact disappear from every dimension-sliced visual.
  • Skip the Silver-count check: a join that fans out would inflate facts and KPIs.
  • Merge before validating: a failed run would leave Gold partially updated across nine tables.
CRITICAL Gold merge, deployed validation & operational views — merge_gold_table, validate_deployed_gold, deploy_operational_views, refresh_gold · src/carewatch/gold.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

refresh_gold orchestrates the whole Gold refresh: stage, validate, MERGE each table in order, validate the deployed tables, and (re)create two operational views for Power BI. merge_gold_table performs a hash-aware MERGE; validate_deployed_gold re-checks the real tables; deploy_operational_views publishes vw_gold_pipeline_runs and vw_gold_errors.

Idempotent, minimal writes: unchanged rows are not touched, new rows are inserted, and for current-state tables rows that no longer exist in Silver are deleted. The privacy check is enforced on the actual Gold tables.

2a · Inputs
  • spark, catalog, schema and an optional audit_record dict that is updated live.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • GoldRefreshResult (rows read/aggregated/inserted/updated/deleted, per-table metrics, table counts).
  • Nine Gold Delta tables merged; two views created or replaced.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. stage_gold_outputs then validate_staged_outputs.
  2. rows_read = sum of Silver counts; rows_aggregated = non-deleted deficiency + penalty facts; both written into the audit record.
  3. For each table in dependency order, MERGE by primary key; update only when business_hash differs; insert new; for current-state tables also delete rows missing from the source (whenNotMatchedBySourceDelete). The audit record is updated after each table.
  4. validate_deployed_gold: no banned (privacy/lineage) columns, no duplicate PKs or NULL load times, no orphan FKs, and exact staged-vs-deployed key sets for current-state tables.
  5. CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW for the run and error views.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 862–895The Gold MERGE. whenMatchedUpdate only if target.business_hash <> source.business_hash; whenNotMatchedInsert for new keys; optional whenNotMatchedBySourceDelete so removed entities disappear. Metrics come from Delta history.
lines 1035–1052Stage, validate, and write the read/aggregated counts to the audit record before any write.
lines 1054–1089The merge loop. delete_missing=name in GOLD_CURRENT_STATE_TABLES (dim_facility, three facts, aggregate). dim_date, dim_geography, dim_deficiency, dim_measure may keep unused members. The nine MERGEs are separate Delta transactions, so they are not atomic across tables; the staging validation exists to make mid-way failure unlikely.
lines 1091–1101After the merges: validate the deployed tables, publish the views, and return the result.
lines 898–924Privacy gate on the deployed tables: telephone_number, provider_address, provider_address_hash, location, raw_record, corrupt_record, source_file and source_file_sha256 may not appear in any Gold table.
lines 949–966Exact key-set equality for current-state tables: nothing missing and nothing stale after the merge.
lines 974–986vw_gold_pipeline_runs exposes the execution log (with a computed duration_seconds) to Power BI's Pipeline Health page.
lines 987–1012vw_gold_errors unions schema-drift rows, Bronze and Silver quarantine rules (exploding failed_rules) and FAILURE log rows into daily counts per dataset, layer and rule.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • stage_gold_outputs, validate_staged_outputs, merge_gold_table, validate_deployed_gold, deploy_operational_views, gold_table_name.
  • Delta DeltaTable.merge, history(1).

Called by: Notebook 04_silver_to_gold cell 3, inside audited(...) (layer Silver-to-Gold, dataset all).

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • Reads Silver; writes Gold and two views.
  • The views read pipeline_execution_logs, schema_drift_log, bronze_quarantine, silver_quarantine.
  • Power BI connects to the nine Gold tables and the two views.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ACTUAL

Evidence for 25 Oct 2026 scheduled run 886646173959938: the Gold audit row has rows_read=698,750 and rows_aggregated=434,330 (= 418,911 + 15,419 active deficiency and penalty facts) and no inserts, updates or deletes because nothing changed in Silver. An OPTIMIZE run on fact_deficiency was a no-op (one file of 30,324,421 bytes). The nine Gold tables total 54,299,045 bytes (all from the repo's evidence documents).

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“Gold is rebuilt as a complete current-state projection every run, but written with hash-aware MERGE, so unchanged rows cost nothing. The nine MERGEs are not one transaction, so we validate everything first and again after deployment. Privacy columns are banned from Gold by an automated check.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Replace MERGE with overwrite: Power BI would see empty tables during refresh and Delta history would show a full rewrite every day.
  • Remove whenNotMatchedBySourceDelete: rows removed in Silver would stay in Gold forever.
  • Remove the banned-column check: a future change could leak address hashes or file paths to the BI layer.
  • Make the views non-replace: a rerun would fail because the views exist.
CRITICAL Notebook 04 and the Databricks Job — notebooks/04_silver_to_gold.ipynb + deployment/carewatch_daily_incremental.job.json · notebooks/04_silver_to_gold.ipynb + deployment/carewatch_daily_incremental.job.json
1 · What it does and why it exists

Notebook 04 wraps refresh_gold in audited(...). The job JSON defines the four-task DAG, the daily schedule and the parameters that tie the tasks together.

This is the automation requirement: one scheduled Job that runs acquisition, Bronze, Silver and Gold in order and stops on the first failure.

2a · Inputs
  • Widgets catalog, schema, load_type, pipeline_run_id.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • One Silver-to-Gold audit row whose batch_id is gold:<pipeline_run_id> and whose parameter_processed JSON lists the successful Silver batch ids and the nine targets.
  • Displayed per-table metrics and counts; a Gold refresh succeeded line.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Look up Silver batch ids that succeeded in this pipeline run (informational, stored in the audit parameter).
  2. Build batch_id = gold:<pipeline_run_id> (or gold:manual:<run_id> when run by hand).
  3. Run refresh_gold(..., audit_record=record) inside audited.
  4. Display the metrics.
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
cell 3, lines 10–27The Gold log's parameter is a compact, sorted JSON string; strategy is explicitly complete_current_silver_state.
cell 3, lines 29–45refresh_gold writes rows_read, rows_aggregated, rows_inserted/updated/deleted straight into the audit record as it goes, so a failure still shows the progress made.
lines 2–8Git-sourced Job (main) running the notebooks from the repository. One run at a time prevents two refreshes racing on the same Delta tables.
lines 17–21Daily at 03:00 UTC (0 0 3 * * ?).
lines 53–71Example task. depends_on + run_if: ALL_SUCCESS create the DAG; {{job.run_id}} becomes the shared pipeline_run_id; only the secret names are in the repository.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • carewatch.audit.audited, carewatch.gold.refresh_gold, successful_silver_batches_for_pipeline_run, GOLD_SCHEMAS.

Called by: Job task silver_to_gold (depends on bronze_to_silver).

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • pipeline_run_id joins the audit rows of all four tasks, which is what the Pipeline Health page filters on.
  • Job-level parameters catalog, schema and load_type (default incremental) are passed to notebooks that declare matching widgets.
  • Evidence: scheduled runs on 24 and 25 Oct 2026 (README/evidence docs): 340.989 s and 489.320 s.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ACTUAL

The 25 Oct 2026 run 886646173959938 took 489.320 s end to end (03:00:08 to 03:08:17 UTC); the four task durations were 103, 76, 62 and 227 seconds. The README evidence prices it at 1.359740075 DBU × USD 0.35 = USD 0.475909 (documented, not recomputed on Databricks). The deployed Job's branch differs from the JSON (codex/fix-phase3-review vs main), a documented discrepancy.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“Four Databricks Job tasks depend on each other with ALL_SUCCESS, run daily at 03:00 UTC, and share a pipeline run id from {{job.run_id}}. If any task raises, later tasks do not run, which stops Gold from publishing on bad data.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Remove depends_on/run_if: Gold could run while Silver is still failing.
  • Allow concurrent runs: two refreshes could interleave MERGEs on the same tables.
  • Hard-code the salt in the JSON: it would be committed to git and visible to every collaborator.
CRITICAL Explicit schemas & contracts — src/carewatch/schemas.py · src/carewatch/schemas.py
1 · What it does and why it exists

The single source of schema truth: source column tuples for the four CMS datasets, the explicit all-string source schemas, the Bronze lineage columns, typed Silver schemas for the four Silver tables, the entity and business keys, the declarative validation specs and the header override map. _validate_contract_constants() runs at import time.

The assignment forbids schema inference. By declaring every schema here, ingestion, setup (00_setup_tables), Silver and Gold all agree on the same contract, and a mismatch fails loudly.

2a · Inputs
  • Imported by almost every module and notebook.
2b · Outputs / side effects
  • SOURCE_COLUMNS, SOURCE_SCHEMAS, CSV_READ_SCHEMAS, BRONZE_SCHEMAS, SILVER_SCHEMAS, SILVER_ENTITY_KEYS, SILVER_BUSINESS_KEYS, SILVER_VALIDATION_SPECS, HEADER_OVERRIDES, accessor functions.
3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Import: build all schemas as module-level constants.
  2. _validate_contract_constants() immediately checks that each dataset has exactly the declared number of columns (24, 14, 102, 23), no duplicates, and every override targets a real column.
  3. Callers use accessors such as source_columns(dataset) and silver_validation_spec(dataset).
4 · Line-by-line explanation of the actual code
lines 211–216The contract's column counts. Also the figures quoted for the four CMS sources.
lines 218–224One explicit CSV-header → API-name mapping that normalisation cannot derive, because CMS truncated the API field name.
lines 235–245The lineage columns added to every Bronze row.
lines 281–291Lineage columns on every Silver row, including row_hash, is_deleted and source_processing_date.
lines 293–323Typed Silver deficiency schema. Non-nullable columns are exactly the business key: CCN, survey date, survey type, prefix, tag and inspection cycle. provider_address_hash replaces the address; there is no phone or location.
lines 1125–1142Fail-fast at import: _validate_contract_constants() is called at module level right after this definition, so a bad column count or override stops every import of the package.
5 · Functions / modules it calls
  • PySpark types only; re, dataclasses.

Called by: bronze, silver, gold, audit, drift (indirectly), notebooks 00, 02, 03, 98, 99.

6 · How it interacts with the rest of the pipeline
  • 00_setup_tables creates Silver and Gold tables from SILVER_SCHEMAS / GOLD_SCHEMAS.
  • notebooks/03 calls require_exact_table_schema against these schemas.
  • bulk_header_mapping in this module is defined but is not called by pipeline code in the current tree; header resolution is done by drift.classify_csv_header.
7 · Realistic project-specific example ACTUAL

SOURCE_COLUMNS['provider_info'] has 102 entries. The local provider CSV header has exactly 102 columns (verified by running classify_csv_header locally: 0 missing, 0 added). The deficiency business key is six columns long, and 418,947 local deficiency rows have 418,947 distinct keys.

8 · How to explain it in the viva
Say this

“schemas.py is the data contract. Every dataset has an explicit schema; nothing is inferred. The column counts are asserted at import, and Silver and Gold tables are created from the same definitions the code uses.”

9 · What breaks if it is modified or removed
  • Edit a column name: Bronze reads, Silver try_cast and Gold selects all fail with analysis errors.
  • Change a count in EXPECTED_SOURCE_COLUMN_COUNTS without changing the tuples: every import of the package raises RuntimeError.
  • Mark a business-key column nullable: rows with a missing key part would get a hash instead of being rejected.
IMPORTANT Notebook 00 — notebooks/00_setup_tables.ipynb · notebooks/00_setup_tables.ipynb
1 · What it does and why it exists

Creates the catalog, schema and landing Volume if they do not exist, then creates the control tables, the four Silver tables and the nine Gold tables with ensure_delta_table.

Run once before the first pipeline run (and once per demo schema). Everything is IF NOT EXISTS / verified, so rerunning it is safe.

2a · Inputs
  • Widgets catalog (default carewatch), schema (pipeline), volume (landing).
2b · Outputs / side effects

3 · Step-by-step execution sequence
  1. Validate every identifier with qualified_name before using it in DDL.
  2. CREATE CATALOG/SCHEMA/VOLUME IF NOT EXISTS.
  3. Collect the result of ensure_control_tables and ensure_delta_table for Silver and Gold.
  4. Display the result and print the landing root.

cell 2, lines 1–15Identifier validation then idempotent DDL.
cell 3, lines 29–55Creates or verifies Silver and Gold tables with their explicit schemas. The last two blocks are the Silver and Gold generator expressions.

98_prepare_drift_demo writes a tiny two-row synthetic Provider Information CSV (one extra column and one row with an invalid rating) into an isolated demo schema and registers it in the manifest. 99_demo_idempotency_drift_backfill is a read-only set of evidence queries for idempotency, drift, backfill scope and Silver results.

They let you demonstrate schema drift, quarantine and idempotency without touching production data. They are demo support, not pipeline code.

E5 · Concept boxes

Five ideas the examiner is almost certain to probe. Each ends with where to find it in the code.

Backfill: re-running history without touching CMS or the watermark

Definition. Reprocessing data that was already registered (a past batch) rather than fetching today's data.

  • Raw → Bronze replay: notebook 02 with dataset, acquisition_run_id (and optionally source_path) plus reprocess=true. Bronze replaces only the rows of the matching deterministic _batch_id (replaceWhere).
  • Bronze → Silver replay: notebook 03 with batch_ids or the ingest_from / ingest_to window and reprocess=true. It reads durable Bronze and never re-contacts CMS.
  • Safety: backfill never advances ingestion_watermarks; the MERGE only updates when the incoming source_processing_date is present and not older than the target, so an old or undated replay cannot overwrite newer current values; soft delete stays off.
  • Honest limit: notebook 01 does not expose an arbitrary historical API window (README says so). AcquisitionRequest has a start_date field, but no widget feeds it.

Find it: c-nb02, c-nb03, c-silver-select, c-silver-merge. DOCUMENTED

Idempotency: the same input twice changes nothing

Definition. Running the pipeline again on identical input leaves every table unchanged (no duplicates, no timestamp churn).

LayerMechanismWhere
AcquireBulk publication key (modified|url) skip → SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED; batch_id = first 24 hex of sha256(dataset|load_type|source_identity|digest) is stable across run foldersacquire.bulk_publication_key, acquire._batch_id
BronzeOnly manifest items without a terminal Bronze log are selected; a rerun with reprocess=true replaces exactly one _batch_idbronze.select_manifest_items, bronze._write_batch
SilverTerminal Silver statuses (SUCCESS, QUARANTINED_PARTIAL) are skipped; MERGE updates only if row_hash differs; quarantine appended through a null-safe anti-joinsilver.merge_silver_batch, silver.append_quarantine_idempotently
GoldHash-aware MERGE on business_hash; unchanged input gives zero inserts/updates/deletesgold.merge_gold_table

Evidence. The 25 Oct run's Gold audit recorded zero mutations on unchanged input (DOCUMENTED). The Silver proof you can run yourself is in section K (demo 3).

Schema drift: the source changes shape

Definition. The CMS file arrives with a different set of columns from the contract in schemas.py.

ClassMeaningOutcome
ADDED_COLUMNHeader present in file, not in contract, name is validLogged to schema_drift_log; Bronze table is extended with mergeSchema; file is accepted
MISSING_COLUMNContract column absent from the fileBreaking: SchemaDriftError after logging; only that file is rejected
RENAMED_OR_UNMAPPED_COLUMNInvalid/reserved/ambiguous header that cannot be mappedBreaking: file rejected after logging

Offline proof (ACTUAL). I ran the repository's own drift.classify_csv_header against the four local CSV headers: 24/14/102/23 columns, 0 missing, 0 added, not breaking. Fixture 1 (add phase2_demo_added_column): 1 added, not breaking. Fixture 2 (drop provider_name, add provider_nm): missing=['provider_name'], added provider_nm, breaking.

Find it: c-drift, c-bronze-process.

Schema evolution: what is allowed to change automatically

Only Bronze evolves automatically, and only for compatible added columns (mergeSchema). Silver and Gold have explicit schemas, so a new Bronze column does not silently reach them (the README requires that CMS schema changes must not silently alter downstream tables). To expose it you change the contract in schemas.py deliberately. INFERRED from the explicit column lists; no end-to-end evolution run exists in the repo's evidence.

Type drift (e.g. a number becomes text) is handled differently: Bronze keeps everything as strings, and Silver's try_cast turns the bad value into a quarantined row with a SAFE_CAST rule label instead of crashing the batch.

Grain: what one row means

Definition. The exact thing one row of a table represents. A wrong grain double-counts everything.

TableOne row is…Key
silver_facility / dim_facilityone nursing home (one CCN)facility_key = sha256 of canonical JSON of the CCN
silver_deficiency / fact_deficiencyone citation (CCN, survey date, survey type, prefix, tag, cycle)deficiency_key
silver_penalty / fact_penaltyone fine or payment denialpenalty_key
silver_mds_quality / fact_mds_qualityone facility × measure × resident type × measure periodmds_key
dim_dateone calendar daydate_key (yyyymmdd int)
dim_geographyone state code plus an unknown memberstate_key
dim_deficiencyone prefix + tag number (+category)deficiency_type_key
dim_measureone measure code + resident typemeasure_key
agg_state_monthly_complianceone state × month(state_key, month_date_key)

Why it matters in the dashboard. dim_facility is SCD Type 1 (current state): the rating next to a 2024 citation is the provider's rating now; the event's date and state come from the fact.

The full Bronze and Silver column-by-column dictionaries (102 provider columns alone) are in the README under “Bronze and Silver data models”. Bronze = source columns as strings + 7 lineage columns. Silver = typed columns + row_hash, is_deleted, source_file, source_file_sha256, source_batch_id, source_processing_date, load_timestamp, with the entity key (facility_key, deficiency_key, penalty_key, mds_key) as primary key.

G5 · Power BI: data path

  1. Power BI Desktop connects to a Databricks SQL warehouse and reads the nine Gold tables plus vw_gold_pipeline_runs and vw_gold_errors (README, “Phase 3”). DOCUMENTED
  2. The README recommends Import refresh after the Gold task succeeds; the actual storage mode is stored in the DataModel binary and was not verified. UNVERIFIED
  3. Gold is not a single transaction across tables, so a refresh while Gold is mid-run could read a mixed state; the README tells you to refresh only after task 4 succeeds.

  • The Quality Overview cards all carry the title “Last 12 Complete Months”, although Current Average Rating is a current value, not a 12-month one.
  • No card shows 4,684 on the Quality Overview page. The 4,684 appears as the matrix total on Facility and Staffing and in the PDF; the Quality Overview card shows “3K” (facilities with serious citations; my local recomputation gives 2,933).

G9 · How to explain every Power BI visual to the evaluator

Use this section when the examiner asks you to open the dashboard and “walk me through each graph.” Screenshots live in G6 and on disk under docs/evidence/phase3/dashboard/. Open BI/CareWatch_Nursing_Homes.pbix if Desktop is available; otherwise point at the evidence PNGs. Numbers below match the ACTUAL captures.

How to use each card

For every visual: say what it is (table + measure), why the page needs it, and the BI decision it supports. Then stop. Do not invent DAX (see G8). Do not invent visuals that are not in the PBIX (no state map, no scatter).

One-line framing before you click any page

“Power BI is the consumption layer on top of Gold. Import refresh runs after the Silver-to-Gold task succeeds. Four report pages answer four questions: national quality pulse, which facilities are worst, clinical MDS measures, and whether the pipeline itself is healthy.”

Page 1 · Quality Overview

Evidence: docs/evidence/phase3/dashboard/quality_overview.png · tables: dim_date, dim_facility, fact_deficiency, fact_penalty, _measures

1A · KPI cards — Facilities with Serious Citations 12M · Fine Dollars 12M · Current Average Rating

Right-hand cards. Capture shows 3K, 95.09M, 2.99. All three cards are titled “Last 12 Complete Months” even though rating is current-state.

What it isThree card visuals bound to measures in _measures: distinct facilities with ≥1 serious citation in the last 12 complete months; sum of fine_amount in that window; average of current dim_facility.overall_rating. Why neededGives the examiner an executive pulse in three numbers before any chart. Serious citations = harm/potential harm (severity G–I / J–L). Fines = financial consequence. Rating = CMS 1–5 star quality signal. BI it tells~3,000 facilities had at least one serious citation; ~$95M in fines; industry average rating sits near 3.0 — middling quality, real regulatory cost.
Say this

“These three cards are the national pulse for the last twelve complete months. About three thousand facilities had a serious citation, fines total roughly ninety-five million dollars, and the current average CMS overall rating is 2.99. Serious means severity groups G through L from Gold. The rating card is a current SCD1 value from dim_facility, even though the card title repeats ‘Last 12 Complete Months’.”

Do not say

“The overview card is 4,684.” That total is the citation count on the Facility & Staffing matrix, not the facilities-with-citations card. Do not claim the rating is a twelve-month average.

1B · Line chart — “Monthly Serious Citations Each Month”

X = dim_date.year_month (Top-N ~18 months). Y = measure Monthly Serious Citations. Capture: peak early 2025 (~700+), dip late 2025, recovery early 2026, sharp drop into 2026-08.

What it isTime series of serious citation counts by survey month from fact_deficiency filtered through dim_date. Why neededKPIs hide seasonality and recent incompleteness. A line shows whether quality pressure is rising, falling, or truncated by an incomplete latest month. BI it tellsSerious citations trended down from the early-2025 peak, with a late-2025 dip and early-2026 rebound. The near-vertical fall at the right edge is likely an incomplete reporting month — treat the last point as provisional, not a sudden national improvement.
Say this

“This line is monthly serious citations over about eighteen months. We peaked above seven hundred early in 2025, then generally declined, with a dip around late 2025 and a rebound into early 2026. The last month drops almost to zero — I treat that as incomplete CMS reporting, not a miracle improvement.”

1C · Clustered / bar chart — “Serious Citations per 100 Facilities” by ownership_type

Axis = dim_facility.ownership_type. Measure wording from Gold dictionary: serious citations in last 12 complete months ÷ distinct currently listed facilities in the group × 100. Capture: For profit – LLC highest (~37); Government – City/county among the lowest shown (~18).

What it isRate chart so ownership groups of different sizes are comparable. Raw counts would unfairly punish large ownership categories. Why neededAnswers “which ownership forms carry more serious-citation risk per facility?” — a policy / oversight question, not just a total. BI it tellsFor-profit LLC and some government ownership types sit at the high end of the rate; city/county government is lower in this capture. Rate normalisation is the point: compare risk density, not absolute volume.
Say this

“This bar is a rate: serious citations per one hundred currently listed facilities, by ownership type. We use a rate so a large ownership group is not automatically ‘worse’ just because it has more homes. In this capture, for-profit LLCs sit near the top of the risk density.”

Page 2 · Facility & Staffing

Evidence: docs/evidence/phase3/dashboard/facility_staffing.png · tables: dim_facility, fact_penalty, fact_deficiency, _measures

2A · Bar chart — “Most Fined Provider in Last 12 Months”

Y = provider_name, X = Fine Dollars 12M. Capture ranks Bridgewood Health Care Center at the top (past ~$0.6M).

What it isProvider-level ranking of summed fines from fact_penalty over the twelve-month window, labelled via dim_facility. Why neededPage 1 is national. This page names the worst financial offenders so an analyst can escalate specific CCNs. BI it tellsA small set of providers accounts for outsized fine dollars. Bridgewood leads this capture — a concrete investigation target, not an anonymous aggregate.
Say this

“This ranking answers ‘who paid the most fines?’ Bridgewood Health Care Center is the top provider in this capture at over six hundred thousand dollars in the last twelve months. That is the drill-down from the ninety-five million national fine total on page 1.”

2B · Matrix — “Facility compliance detail”

Rows = provider_name. Columns = Serious Citations 12M, Fine Dollars 12M, average overall_rating. Capture total row: 4,684 citations · 95,091,711.00 fines · 2.99 rating. Many top-fined rows show rating 1.00.

What it isTabular join of compliance volume, financial penalty, and current star rating per facility — the evidence grid behind the ranking bar. Why neededBars show order; the matrix proves the numbers and lets you spot the citation–fine–rating pattern (high fines + low stars). BI it tells4,684 serious citations align with ~$95.09M fines (same national fine scale as page 1). Top offenders often sit at 1-star — regulatory pain and quality rating move together in this view.
Say this

“The matrix is the detail view. The total row is four thousand six hundred eighty-four serious citations and about ninety-five million in fines — that is where the 4,684 figure comes from, not from the page-1 facilities card. Many of the heaviest-fined homes show a one-star overall rating.”

2C · Column chart — “Average current nurse staffing by overall rating”

X = overall rating 1–5. Y = average nurse staffing hours (from dim_facility current attributes). Capture: clear step-up from ~3.5 at 1-star toward >4 at 5-star.

What it isAssociation chart between CMS star rating and reported nurse staffing level on the current facility dimension (SCD1). Why neededLinks operations (staffing) to the quality signal (stars). Completes the page story: fines/citations (bad outcomes) vs staffing (an operational lever). BI it tellsHigher-rated homes show higher average staffing in this model. That supports the narrative that staffing and measured quality move together — correlation in the Gold snapshot, not a proven causal study.
Say this

“This column chart relates current nurse staffing to the CMS overall rating. One-star homes sit lower on staffing; five-star homes sit higher. I present it as an association in our Gold snapshot, not as a causal claim that hiring automatically raises the star.”

Do not say

“Staffing causes the rating” or “we proved causality.” Also do not invent a scatter plot — the proposal mentioned one; this PBIX uses a column chart.

Page 3 · MDS Quality

Evidence: docs/evidence/phase3/dashboard/mds_single_period.png · tables: dim_measure, dim_date, fact_mds_quality, _measures. Known cosmetic bug: the textbox title still says “Facility & Staffing”.

3A · Line chart — “Selected MDS measure over time”

Capture shows one point at 2026-03 (~3.25 on the axis). Intended as a multi-period trend; Gold currently exposes a single measure period in this import.

What it isAverage MDS score (MDS Average Score) for the slicer-selected measure, plotted on dim_date via fact_mds_quality.period_end_date_key. Why neededMDS (Minimum Data Set) is clinical quality — falls, antipsychotics, vaccines, etc. — separate from survey citations and fines. Regulators and chains watch these outcome rates. BI it tellsIn this evidence capture it is a single-period cross-section, not a trend. The visual is ready for multiple periods; the imported Gold only supplies one period end (2026-03).
Say this

“This chart is meant to track one MDS clinical measure over time. In the saved evidence we only have one period — March 2026 — so I call it a cross-section, not a trend. When more measure periods land in Gold, the same visual will show the line.”

Do not say

“MDS shows improvement/decline over time” while pointing at a one-point chart.

3B · Card — “Contributing facilities” (MDS Contributing Facilities = 14K)
What it isDistinct facilities with a score for the selected MDS measure (MDS Contributing Facilities). Why neededTells the examiner the average is not based on a handful of homes — scale and coverage of the clinical metric. BI it tells~14,000 facilities contribute to the selected measure in this capture — national MDS coverage, not a local sample.
Say this

“The card says about fourteen thousand facilities contribute to the selected MDS measure, so the average is a national clinical signal, not a tiny sample.”

3C · Slicer — measure_description (single-select)

Capture selection: Percentage of long-stay residents experiencing one or more falls with major injury. List also includes antipsychotics, vaccines, restraints, weight loss, catheters, etc.

What it isSingle-select filter on dim_measure.measure_description that rebinds the line and the contributing-facilities card. Why neededOne page covers many CMS quality measures without duplicating charts. The examiner can ask you to switch measures live. BI it tellsInteractive clinical lens: pick a risk (falls, antipsychotics, …) and read that measure’s national average and coverage. Demonstrate the slicer if asked.
Say this

“The slicer is the clinical lens. I pick a measure description from dim_measure — in this screenshot, falls with major injury — and the average and facility count recompute for that measure only.”

Do not say

Ignore the wrong page title. If asked, admit it: “The textbox title was copied from Facility & Staffing; the page is MDS Quality.”

Page 4 · Pipeline Health & Data Quality

Evidence: docs/evidence/phase3/dashboard/pipeline_health_data_quality.png · tables: disconnected vw_gold_pipeline_runs, vw_gold_errors. Capture: 53 runs · 42 errors (stale vs later audit counts — see section L).

4A · KPI cards — Total Runs · Total Errors
What it isCount of run_id from vw_gold_pipeline_runs; sum of error_count from vw_gold_errors. Why neededProves the warehouse is observed, not only the nursing-home content. Engineering health is part of the assignment story. BI it tellsIn this capture, 53 logged runs and 42 error records — the acquisition edge is noisy; always quote the capture date and admit the PBIX can be stale versus live audit tables.
Say this

“These cards come from the Gold monitoring views over pipeline_execution_logs and the error view. This screenshot shows fifty-three runs and forty-two errors. I treat the numbers as the Import snapshot, not a live query — the 25 October audit view had a different run count after later jobs.”

4B · Stacked bar — “Execution records by layer and status”

Layers: CMS-to-Landing, Raw-to-Bronze, Bronze-to-Silver, Silver-to-Gold. Statuses include SUCCESS, FAILURE, SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED, QUARANTINED_PARTIAL.

What it isDistribution of audit statuses per Medallion layer from vw_gold_pipeline_runs. Why neededShows where the pipeline hurts. A flat “42 errors” card does not say whether Bronze failed or acquisition skipped. BI it tellsCMS-to-Landing carries most FAILURE and SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED (idempotent re-acquires). Raw-to-Bronze is largely SUCCESS. Bronze-to-Silver / Silver-to-Gold show QUARANTINED_PARTIAL when bad rows were isolated without failing the whole batch.
Say this

“This stacked bar is the health breakdown by layer. Acquisition shows failures and skips — skips mean we already had that window. Bronze is mostly success. Quarantined-partial on Silver or Gold means we kept good rows and isolated bad ones, which is intentional data-quality behaviour, not a silent drop.”

4C · Detail table — run log (time, layer, status, duration, rows_*)

Capture example: Bronze-to-Silver on 2026-10-10 with status QUARANTINED_PARTIAL, 36 rows_quarantined, ~62s duration; several CMS-to-Landing FAILURE rows with 0 rows read.

What it isRow-level audit: Year/Month/Day hierarchy on start time, pipeline_layer, status, duration_seconds, rows_read, rows_aggregated, rows_quarantined. Why neededRoot-cause evidence for the cards and stacked bar. Examiner can ask “show me a quarantine event.” BI it tellsConcrete proof that quarantine counts are logged (36 rows in that Silver run) and that failed acquisitions read zero rows — lineage and operability, not only analytics.
Say this

“The table is the audit log in Gold. Here a Bronze-to-Silver run quarantined thirty-six rows and still finished as quarantined-partial. Failed CMS-to-Landing rows show zero rows read — that is how we prove the control plane is wired into Power BI.”

Do not say

“We chart errors by rule or dataset.” vw_gold_errors has those columns, but this page has no error-by-rule visual.

Model view · Star schema relationships

Evidence: docs/evidence/phase3/dashboard/power_bi_model_view.png · detail table in G7

M · Relationship diagram (not a report page, but examiners ask)
What it isPower BI Model view: dimensions (dim_facility, dim_date, dim_geography, dim_deficiency, dim_measure) filter facts (fact_deficiency, fact_penalty, fact_mds_quality) and agg_state_monthly_compliance with 1:* single-direction relationships on surrogate keys. _measures, vw_gold_pipeline_runs, and vw_gold_errors sit disconnected. Why neededExplains why slicers on facility/date/ownership correctly filter citation and fine visuals, and why the Pipeline page does not filter the quality pages (and vice versa). BI it tellsClassic star schema for analytics; monitoring views are intentionally isolated so pipeline ops KPIs do not get sliced by a nursing-home dimension by accident.
Say this

“In Model view you see a star: dimensions on the outside, facts in the middle, one-to-many, single-direction. Facts are never joined to each other. The two pipeline views and the measures table are disconnected on purpose so Pipeline Health stays an ops page.”

90-second dashboard tour (memorise this)

Speak this while clicking pages 1 → 4

“Page 1 is the national pulse: three KPIs, a monthly serious-citation trend, and a per-100-facilities rate by ownership so large ownership groups are fair. Page 2 drills to named providers — who was fined most — with a matrix that totals 4,684 serious citations and about 95 million dollars, plus staffing rising with star rating. Page 3 is MDS clinical quality with a measure slicer; in our evidence it is a single March 2026 period across about 14 thousand facilities, and the title textbox is a known cosmetic bug. Page 4 is pipeline ops from the audit views: run and error counts, status by Medallion layer, and a row-level log that shows quarantined rows. Refresh Power BI only after Gold task 4 succeeds so Import does not read a half-merged star.”

If the examiner only wants business insight

Lead with pages 1–3 (quality, money, staffing, clinical MDS). Keep page 4 for “how do you know the data is trustworthy?” — that is where CareWatch’s engineering story lands in BI.

J · Architectural decisions

Why each design choice was made, what it costs, what else was possible. Tagged DOCUMENTED when a repo document states it, INTERPRETATION when I reconstructed the reason from the code.

  • Open any decision for choice, reason, benefits, trade-offs, alternatives, limitations and the file to point at.
  • In a viva always name the trade-off yourself; it shows you understood the choice.
Bronze keeps every column as a string DOCUMENTED
AspectDetail
ChoiceAll source columns are read with explicit string schemas; lineage columns are appended.
WhyNo type error can fail ingestion, and the raw value stays available for audit (proposal: “ingested strictly as a string to eliminate ingestion failures”).
BenefitsNever loses a source value; schema drift is easy to see.
Trade-offsDisk and query cost; typing deferred to Silver.
AlternativesTyped Bronze with infer or permissive nulls (rejected: forbidden by the assignment and hides bad values).
LimitationsBronze holds clear-text address and telephone.
Whereschemas.py; bronze.py
Manifest-driven processing DOCUMENTED
AspectDetail
ChoiceNotebooks 02 and 03 read source_file_manifest and the logs, never the folder.
WhyDirectory listings cannot tell a complete download from a partial one; the manifest records size and SHA-256.
BenefitsSafe retries, exact backfills, integrity verification before reading.
Trade-offsOne more table to keep consistent.
AlternativesList the Volume and compare timestamps.
LimitationsA manifest row without a file fails that item, by design.
Wherebronze.select_manifest_items, verify_landing_file
Deterministic batch_id and replaceWhere DOCUMENTED
AspectDetail
Choicebatch_id = sha256 of dataset|load_type|source_identity|digest, first 24 hex characters; Bronze rewrites only that batch.
WhyA rerun must replace itself, not append a duplicate (README requirement 8).
BenefitsIdempotent Bronze; independent reprocessing per batch.
Trade-offsA hash collision would merge batches (practically negligible at 96 bits).
AlternativesRandom UUID per run (rejected: reruns would duplicate).
LimitationsBatch id depends on source identity text; a changed URL creates a new batch.
Whereacquire._batch_id, bronze._write_batch
Watermark moves only after full reconciliation DOCUMENTED
AspectDetail
Choicereconcile_acquisition_run commits the watermark; Gold and Silver never move it.
WhyA partly loaded window must never hide the missing days.
BenefitsNo silent gaps; failure leaves the window pending.
Trade-offsA single bad file blocks the dataset's watermark.
AlternativesAdvance on download (rejected: loses rows on failure).
LimitationsIncremental fails until a successful full load exists.
Wherebronze.reconcile_acquisition_run, watermarks.commit_bronze_watermark
60-day overlap on API windows DOCUMENTED
AspectDetail
ChoiceEach incremental starts at watermark − overlap_days (default 60).
WhyCMS can add or revise records late; the proposal specified a 60-day safety overlap.
BenefitsCatches late changes cheaply.
Trade-offsRe-reads about two months each day; relies on MERGE for dedupe.
AlternativesStrict watermark (misses late changes); full reload (costly).
LimitationsChanges older than 60 days are not seen until the next full snapshot.
Whereacquire.resolve_window_start
Hash keys and row hashes with MERGE DOCUMENTED
AspectDetail
ChoiceEntity key = sha256 of canonical JSON of the business key; row_hash = sha256 of the typed row.
WhyStable surrogate keys that need no sequence and detect real change.
BenefitsIdempotent merges; Gold can reuse Silver keys.
Trade-offsHashes are opaque to humans; key columns cannot change without new keys.
AlternativesIdentity/sequence keys; compare every column.
LimitationsHash equality of Spark and Python JSON is INFERRED only.
Wheresilver.sha256_json_columns, merge_silver_batch
SCD Type 1 provider profile DOCUMENTED
AspectDetail
Choicedim_facility shows the current profile only.
WhyThe CMS provider file is a current snapshot; the PDF names dim_facility “current-state SCD1”.
BenefitsSimple model, small dimension.
Trade-offsA 2023 citation sits next to today's rating and ownership.
AlternativesSCD2 or fact_facility_snapshot (proposed, not built).
LimitationsNo history of rating or ownership changes.
Wheregold.build_dim_facility; PDF p.6
Row-level Silver quarantine, file-level Bronze rejection DOCUMENTED
AspectDetail
ChoiceBad values quarantine one row; missing columns or unreadable envelopes reject the file.
WhyA single bad cell should not stop 418,947 good rows; a missing column breaks the contract for the whole file.
BenefitsPartial success with an audit trail (QUARANTINED_PARTIAL).
Trade-offsQuarantine tables must be monitored.
AlternativesFail the whole batch on any error.
LimitationsThe dashboard has no error-by-rule view.
Wheresilver rules; bronze.process_manifest_item
Privacy boundary at Silver DOCUMENTED
AspectDetail
ChoiceAddress hashed with a salt fetched inside Spark; telephone, address and location dropped; Gold bans them.
WhyThe salt never reaches the driver or Git; Gold is safe to share.
BenefitsNo PII in analytics layers.
Trade-offsLanding and Bronze keep clear text, so their access must be restricted.
AlternativesHash at ingestion (rejected: Bronze should preserve source).
LimitationsDatabricks secret redaction is best-effort (README).
Wheresilver.databricks_secret_expression; gold.validate_deployed_gold
Soft deletes disabled by default DOCUMENTED
AspectDetail
Choiceallow_soft_deletes=false; a dozen guards even when enabled.
WhyA missing row in an API window or filtered scope does not mean deletion.
BenefitsNo accidental mass deletion.
Trade-offsGenuine CMS removals do not propagate unless enabled.
AlternativesAlways delete rows missing from a snapshot.
LimitationsNever exercised in production evidence.
Wheresilver.evaluate_soft_delete
Gold rebuilt from complete current Silver, then MERGE DOCUMENTED
AspectDetail
ChoiceStage all outputs, validate, merge; current-state tables delete rows absent from the source.
WhyA deterministic full rebuild is simpler and safer than change tracking at 51 MiB.
BenefitsConvergent, self-healing; unchanged retry gives zero mutations.
Trade-offsReads all of Silver every run (Gold audit: 698,750 rows read; the whole-run timeline panel reports 12.9 M rows read across all tasks).
AlternativesIncremental Gold from Silver deltas.
LimitationsCost grows with data size.
Wheregold.refresh_gold, merge_gold_table
Nine MERGEs are not one transaction DOCUMENTED
AspectDetail
ChoiceEach Gold table commits separately; validation before and after.
WhyDelta has no multi-table transaction.
BenefitsSimple, retry-safe.
Trade-offsA failure can leave Gold tables out of step until retried.
AlternativesSwap whole schema or views over versioned tables.
LimitationsBI refresh must wait for task success.
Wheregold.merge_gold_table; PDF p.6
Unpartitioned Delta; no routine OPTIMIZE DOCUMENTED
AspectDetail
ChoiceNo partition columns or clustering.
Why51.78 MiB of Gold would become small files; the OPTIMIZE trial rewrote nothing.
BenefitsFewer small files.
Trade-offsNo measured read speed-up either way.
AlternativesPartition facts by year or liquid-cluster on keys.
LimitationsLatency impact was never measured.
WherePDF p.6; spark_finops_2026-10-25.md
Event state versus current state DOCUMENTED
AspectDetail
ChoiceState on a fact comes from the event; ownership and rating come from dim_facility.
WhyFacility profile and event location may differ in time.
BenefitsHonest semantics.
Trade-offsMixed analyses need a stated caveat.
AlternativesStore a snapshot of the profile on each event.
LimitationsEasy to misread in the dashboard.
WherePDF p.6; README Phase 3
pipeline_execution_logs is both audit log and checkpoint INTERPRETATION
AspectDetail
ChoiceSelection logic reads terminal statuses from the log.
WhyOne source of truth for what has completed.
BenefitsNo separate checkpoint store.
Trade-offsDeleting or editing logs changes what reruns.
AlternativesA dedicated state table.
LimitationsLog retention must be managed carefully.
Wheresilver.select_silver_work_items
Same-date update tie rule INTERPRETATION
AspectDetail
ChoiceMERGE updates when the incoming source_processing_date is not null and is not older than the target.
WhyAllows a same-day correction while blocking old data.
BenefitsSimple and monotone.
Trade-offsTwo different rows with the same processing date: the later one processed wins.
AlternativesStrictly newer only; version column.
LimitationsConflict inside one batch is quarantined, but across batches on the same date it is order-dependent.
Wheresilver.should_apply_change

Do every WRITES demo in the separate schema phase2_demo (notebook 98 enforces this), and rehearse them beforehand. None of these steps was executed while producing this guide. K8 · Troubleshooting table

Symptom / messageLikely causeWhat to do
No successful Bronze extraction watermark exists…Incremental run before any full load reached BronzeRun full load through notebook 02 first (by design).
Acquire status SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIREDSame CMS publication already landed (key modified|url)Expected and healthy. Use force_refresh=true only to re-download deliberately.

Why this section exists
