M · Viva questions and answers

54 questions in nine categories. Open a question, read the strong answer, then the deeper explanation. Use the quiz toggle in the sidebar to hide answers and practise.

Q1ConceptualWhat is the Medallion architecture, and why did you use it?
Strong answer
Three layers of increasing quality. Bronze keeps the source exactly as received, plus lineage. Silver is typed, validated, privacy-treated and de-duplicated. Gold is a business-ready star schema. Each layer can be rebuilt from the previous one, so a bug is fixed by replaying, not re-downloading.
Deeper explanation
In CareWatch Bronze is all strings with seven lineage columns, Silver merges by hashed entity key, Gold is nine tables for Power BI.
Where in the repo README “Architecture”; section B
Likely follow-up “Why not go straight from CSV to Gold?” Because you could not audit a rejected value or replay a fix.
Q2ConceptualWhy is Bronze stored as strings?
Strong answer
So that ingestion can never fail on a bad value and the original text is preserved. Typing and validation are moved to Silver where failures become quarantined rows instead of crashes.
Deeper explanation
The proposal states every column is ingested strictly as a string. Silver uses try_cast, so 'not_an_integer' becomes null and the rule SAFE_CAST:overall_rating->overall_rating rejects the row.
Where in the repo docs/data_analysis_project_proposal.md; silver._try_cast
Likely follow-up “Doesn't that waste space?” Yes, accepted for fidelity.
Q3ConceptualWhat does idempotent mean here and how do you prove it?
Strong answer
Running the pipeline twice on the same input leaves the tables unchanged: no duplicate rows and no timestamp churn. Silver and Gold MERGE on a deterministic key and update only when the row hash differs. Proof: the 25 Oct Gold audit recorded zero inserts, updates and deletes on unchanged input, and the Silver rerun demo (K5) should show rows_inserted=0, rows_updated=0.
Deeper explanation
Bronze is idempotent through the deterministic batch_id with replaceWhere; the acquire step skips unchanged publications (SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED).
Where in the repo silver.merge_silver_batch; gold.merge_gold_table; spark_finops_2026-10-25.md
Likely follow-up “What exactly is the key?” See the key question below.
Q4ConceptualExplain full load versus incremental load in your project.
Strong answer
Full load downloads each CMS bulk CSV. Incremental differs by dataset: deficiencies and penalties call the API for a date window starting at the last committed watermark minus 60 days; provider and MDS are snapshots: a new bulk CSV is downloaded only if CMS published a new version, and only changed rows merge.
Deeper explanation
api_date_window versus snapshot_diff in config.DATASETS. Page size is 500 rows.
Where in the repo config.py; acquire.py
Likely follow-up “Why snapshot for provider?” CMS gives no change feed for it.
Q5ConceptualWhat is a watermark and why is there an overlap?
Strong answer
A watermark is the highest source date already safely loaded. It moves only after the whole acquisition run is validated in Bronze. The overlap (60 days) re-reads recent days because CMS can add or revise records late; MERGE absorbs the duplicates.
Deeper explanation
Only bronze.reconcile_acquisition_run commits it (through watermarks.commit_bronze_watermark). If none exists the incremental run fails on purpose.
Where in the repo watermarks.py; acquire.resolve_window_start
Likely follow-up “What if a change is 90 days old?” Not seen until a new snapshot (a stated limitation).
Q6ConceptualWhat kinds of schema drift do you handle and how?
Strong answer
Three classes. An added column is logged and Bronze evolves (mergeSchema). A missing column or an unmappable header is breaking: it is logged and that file is rejected with SchemaDriftError. A type change is not a header issue: Bronze keeps strings and Silver quarantines the rows that fail the cast.
Deeper explanation
I ran the repo's classifier locally: the four real headers give 0 missing and 0 added; a fixture with an extra column gives ADDED_COLUMN; dropping provider_name while adding provider_nm is breaking.
Where in the repo drift.py; bronze.process_manifest_item
Likely follow-up “Does the new column reach Gold?” No, not until the contract is changed deliberately.
Q7ConceptualWhat is a star schema and what is the grain of each fact?
Strong answer
Facts hold measurable events; dimensions hold descriptive attributes. fact_deficiency = one citation, fact_penalty = one fine or payment denial, fact_mds_quality = one facility/measure/period. Dimensions: facility, date, geography, deficiency type, measure.
Deeper explanation
Power BI uses one-to-many, single-direction relationships from each dimension to the facts.
Where in the repo gold.GOLD_SCHEMAS; section G
Likely follow-up “Why isn't dim_facility joined to the aggregate?” The aggregate is by state and month only.
Q8ConceptualWhat is quarantine and when does a row go there?
Strong answer
A holding table for rejected records with the reason. Bronze quarantines corrupt CSV lines (CORRUPT_CSV_RECORD). Silver quarantines rows that fail a rule (required, safe-cast, domain, regex, range, conditional) or that conflict on a business key (CONFLICTING_BUSINESS_KEY). Valid rows continue.
Deeper explanation
In the real data exactly 36 deficiency rows fail the rule CONDITIONAL:correction_date_required; 418,947 − 36 = 418,911 = Gold fact_deficiency.
Where in the repo silver._validation_rule_expressions; bronze_quarantine, silver_quarantine
Likely follow-up “Why not fix them?” We never invent values; the rule says a corrected citation needs a date.
Q9Code-levelWalk me through audited().
Strong answer
It is a context manager. It builds a log record with status SUCCESS and zeroed counts, yields it so the caller fills rows_read, rows_inserted, etc., then on exit: if rows were quarantined and status is SUCCESS it becomes QUARANTINED_PARTIAL; on an exception it becomes FAILURE with a truncated message and the exception is re-raised; in finally it stamps the end time and writes the log row.
Deeper explanation
If writing the log itself fails while a processing error is pending, it prints a warning and preserves the original error. A suppress flag lets a caller skip the success log.
Where in the repo audit.py:audited (lines 292–347)
Likely follow-up “Why re-raise?” So Databricks marks the task failed and downstream tasks do not run.
Q10Code-levelHow is batch_id computed and why?
Strong answer
First 24 hex characters of the SHA-256 of dataset|load_type|source_identity|digest. It is deterministic and does not include the run folder, so the same publication always gets the same id.
Deeper explanation
That lets Bronze replaceWhere _batch_id replace exactly one batch on a rerun.
Where in the repo acquire._batch_id; bronze._write_batch
Likely follow-up “Collision risk?” 96 bits: negligible.
Q11Code-levelHow does the Silver MERGE decide to update a row?
Strong answer
Insert if the key is new. Update only if the incoming row_hash differs (or the target is soft-deleted) AND the incoming source_processing_date is present and not older than the target's. Identical rows are skipped, so their load_timestamp never changes.
Deeper explanation
The date guard stops an old or undated backfill overwriting current SCD1 values.
Where in the repo silver.merge_silver_batch; should_apply_change
Likely follow-up “What if two rows have the same date?” The later processed wins (tie policy).
Q12Code-levelHow are entity keys generated?
Strong answer
SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the business-key columns, e.g. facility key = sha256 of {"cms_certification_number_ccn":"145239"} = 13e87de1…2ce0e2. Gold copies the key from Silver, so there is no join to look up surrogates.
Deeper explanation
Spark uses to_json(struct(...), ignoreNullFields=false) then sha2(…,256); Python mirrors it in canonical_json_sha256. I reproduced the key for CCN 145239 with the repo helper. Spark/Python byte-equality is inferred, not tested.
Where in the repo silver.sha256_json_columns, canonical_json_sha256
Likely follow-up “What if a key column is null?” Required rules reject such rows first.
Q13Code-levelHow is the address hashed without exposing the salt?
Strong answer
sha2(upper(address) + secret(scope, key), 256) is evaluated inside Spark using Databricks SQL secret(). The Python driver sees only the scope and key names (carewatch-address-hashing, salt-v1), never the value.
Deeper explanation
The code never selects or logs the expression because secret redaction is best-effort. Telephone, address and location are then dropped.
Where in the repo silver.databricks_secret_expression; Job JSON
Likely follow-up “What if the salt rotates?” Every provider_address_hash changes, so every row_hash changes and the next merge updates all rows (inferred); Gold is unaffected because it holds no hash.
Q14Code-levelHow does Bronze verify a file before reading it?
Strong answer
verify_landing_file compares the file's size and SHA-256 with the manifest row; a mismatch raises IntegrityError. Only manifest items with successful status and no terminal Bronze log are selected, so unregistered files are never read.
Deeper explanation
Download itself streams to a .partial file, hashes while writing and only then os.replaces it.
Where in the repo bronze.verify_landing_file; acquire._stream_to_temporary_file
Likely follow-up “What if the manifest is wrong?” Then Bronze fails that item; nothing downstream runs.
Q15Code-levelHow does append_quarantine_idempotently avoid duplicates?
Strong answer
It left-anti-joins the new quarantine rows to the existing table on the identifying columns using null-safe equality, and appends only rows not already present, so a retry does not double-write rejects.
Deeper explanation
That is why silver_quarantine can be rewritten on retry without growing.
Where in the repo silver.append_quarantine_idempotently
Likely follow-up “And rows_quarantined in the log?” It is the rows rejected in this execution, not the number newly appended.
Q16Code-levelHow does Gold decide which rows to delete?
Strong answer
For the current-state tables (dim_facility, the three facts and the aggregate) the MERGE uses whenNotMatchedBySourceDelete, so a row that disappeared from the rebuilt source is deleted. A soft-deleted Silver event remains in its fact with is_deleted=true; the aggregate excludes it.
Deeper explanation
Dimensions like date, geography, deficiency and measure are not in GOLD_CURRENT_STATE_TABLES, so they are never deleted by the merge.
Where in the repo gold.merge_gold_table; GOLD_CURRENT_STATE_TABLES
Likely follow-up “Why keep deleted facts?” Visibility; BI filters on is_deleted.
Q17Code-levelWhat does validate_staged_outputs check?
Strong answer
Before any merge: exact column sets, PK null and duplicate counts, fact row counts against Silver, FK resolution by left anti-join, and the aggregate's reconciliation to the facts (six totals). A failure raises GoldValidationError and nothing merges.
Deeper explanation
After merging, validate_deployed_gold checks the real tables, key sets and bans privacy columns.
Where in the repo gold.validate_staged_outputs; validate_deployed_gold
Likely follow-up “Why do this in code?” Delta does not enforce PK/FK.
Q18ArchitectureWhy four separate notebooks rather than one?
Strong answer
Each layer has its own failure boundary, parameters and audit rows, and can be rerun alone (backfill). The Job chains them with ALL_SUCCESS, so a failed upstream task stops the rest.
Deeper explanation
Notebooks are thin drivers; all logic lives in src/carewatch so it is readable and importable.
Where in the repo Job JSON; notebooks/
Likely follow-up “Isn't that overhead?” Each task needs its own cluster start, as the 103/76/62/227 s task times show.
Q19ArchitectureWhy drive processing from a manifest instead of listing folders?
Strong answer
A folder listing cannot say whether a file is complete, which run produced it or what it should contain. The manifest stores path, size, SHA-256, strategy, window and expected rows, and the logs say what already succeeded.
Deeper explanation
This also makes backfill exact: you name a batch_id.
Where in the repo source_file_manifest; bronze.select_manifest_items
Likely follow-up “Single point of failure?” It is a Delta table with history.
Q20ArchitectureWhere does PII live and how is it handled in each layer?
Strong answer
Landing and Bronze contain clear-text address and telephone (source fidelity). Silver drops telephone, address and location and stores a salted SHA-256 of the address. Gold has none of them and a runtime check bans them. Monitoring views expose counts only.
Deeper explanation
So access to the landing Volume and Bronze must be restricted; that is a stated limitation.
Where in the repo silver.transform_bronze_batch; gold.validate_deployed_gold
Likely follow-up “Why not hash earlier?” Bronze must preserve source for audit.
Q21ArchitectureHow does Power BI connect and how is the model built?
Strong answer
Through a Databricks SQL warehouse to the Gold tables and two monitoring views. Dimension-to-fact one-to-many, single-direction relationships; facts are not joined to each other; the monitoring views and _measures are disconnected tables.
Deeper explanation
The README recommends Import and refreshing after Gold finishes; the storage mode is not verifiable from the file.
Where in the repo BI/…pbix; section G
Likely follow-up “Why not DirectQuery?” Not decided in the repo; I would say Import avoids warehouse cost per interaction (interpretation).
Q22ArchitectureDescribe the Job configuration.
Strong answer
“CareWatch Daily Incremental”: four Git-sourced notebook tasks in a chain with run_if: ALL_SUCCESS, cron 0 0 3 * * ? UTC, one concurrent run with queueing, parameters catalog, schema, load_type, and pipeline_run_id={{job.run_id}} in every task for traceability.
Deeper explanation
Secret scope and key names are passed to the Silver task; the salt value is not in Git.
Where in the repo deployment/carewatch_daily_incremental.job.json
Likely follow-up “Why one concurrent run?” Two runs would write the same tables.
Q23ArchitectureHow does one pipeline run get traced across layers?
Strong answer
The Job passes {{job.run_id}} as pipeline_run_id to all tasks, and each audited unit writes it into pipeline_execution_logs. Gold also writes batch_id='gold:<run id>'. The acceptance query in the README filters by it.
Deeper explanation
vw_gold_pipeline_runs exposes it to Power BI.
Where in the repo audit.py; README acceptance query
Q24Code-modificationHow would you add a fifth CMS dataset?
Strong answer
Add a DatasetConfig to config.DATASETS (id, strategy, watermark, Bronze/Silver names); add its source columns, Silver schema, keys and validation spec to schemas.py; add a Gold builder and schema if it feeds the model. Notebook dropdowns read sorted(DATASETS), so they update themselves.
Deeper explanation
schemas._validate_contract_constants() runs at import and fails fast if the contract is inconsistent.
Where in the repo config.py; schemas.py; gold.py
Likely follow-up “What else?” Add to the Job parameters if it needs custom settings (inferred).
Q25Code-modificationCMS adds a new column. How do you get it into Silver and Gold?
Strong answer
Bronze already evolves. Then add the column to the Bronze/Silver contracts in schemas.py and the Silver spec, migrate the Silver table (setup verifies the exact schema and fails otherwise), and add it to the Gold schema and builder if needed.
Deeper explanation
All Silver row_hash values change because the hashed struct changes, so the next merge updates every row (inferred).
Where in the repo schemas.py; silver.require_exact_table_schema
Likely follow-up “Is that safe?” It is intentional; the alternative is silent schema change, which the README forbids.
Q26Code-modificationHow would you change the overlap from 60 to 30 days?
Strong answer
Change the overlap_days base parameter in the Job JSON (and the widget default if needed) and redeploy; the code reads it as a parameter.
Deeper explanation
No code change. Remember the trade-off: fewer re-read days but a smaller window for catching late revisions.
Where in the repo Job JSON; notebooks/01
Q27Code-modificationHow would you turn dim_facility into SCD Type 2?
Strong answer
Add effective-from/to dates and a current flag, make the dimension key version-specific, and change the Gold merge from overwrite-style to close-and-insert. Facts must then join to the version valid at the event date.
Deeper explanation
That would also let the dashboard show a 2023 citation with the 2023 rating, which today it cannot.
Where in the repo gold.build_dim_facility
Likely follow-up “Cost?” More rows and a point-in-time join in BI.
Q28Code-modificationHow would you partition fact_deficiency?
Strong answer
Add a derived partition column such as survey year in the table creation and the builder, include it in the MERGE condition so Delta can prune files, then measure.
Deeper explanation
I would not, at 30 MB: the PDF argues small files would result.
Where in the repo 00_setup_tables; PDF p.6

Q29Failure / recoveryGold fails after four of the nine MERGEs. What happens?
Strong answer
The task is marked failed and a FAILURE audit row is written. Gold is temporarily out of step because tables commit separately. Rerun task 4: staging is rebuilt from complete Silver, already merged tables produce zero changes, and the remaining ones merge. Refresh Power BI only after it succeeds.
Deeper explanation
This is exactly the README's “retry-safe but not a cross-table transaction”.
Where in the repo gold.refresh_gold; README Phase 3
Likely follow-up “Could BI read a mixed state?” Yes, if refreshed in between; hence the rule.
Q30Failure / recoveryThe CMS download is cut off halfway.
Strong answer
The bytes are written to a .partial file and renamed only after completion, with up to three attempts. A manifest row is written only for a completed file; Bronze also verifies size and SHA-256, so a truncated file cannot be read.
Deeper explanation
The run fails; the watermark does not move.
Where in the repo acquire._stream_to_temporary_file; bronze.verify_landing_file
Q31Failure / recoveryThe same file is delivered twice.
Strong answer
For bulk files the publication key modified|url matches and acquisition is logged as SKIPPED_ALREADY_ACQUIRED. If it were landed again anyway, the identical digest gives the same batch_id, Bronze/Silver see a terminal log and skip it, and MERGE would change nothing.
Deeper explanation
This is what the 25 Oct run shows for provider and MDS.
Where in the repo acquire.bulk_publication_key
Q32Failure / recoveryA new CMS file is missing a column.
Strong answer
The header is classified MISSING_COLUMN; it is logged to schema_drift_log, SchemaDriftError is raised and that file is rejected. Raw-to-Bronze raises, so Silver and Gold tasks do not run, and the watermark does not advance.
Deeper explanation
Nothing partial reaches Bronze.
Where in the repo drift.py; bronze.process_manifest_item
Likely follow-up “How do you recover?” Update the contract or wait for CMS, then rerun.
Q33Failure / recoveryCMS removes a provider from its file. What happens?
Strong answer
With allow_soft_deletes=false (the production setting) nothing: the Silver and Gold rows remain and is_currently_listed stays true. Enabling soft delete is gated by strict conditions (complete, validated, newest snapshot, no quarantine).
Deeper explanation
This is a known limitation: removals are not propagated by default.
Where in the repo silver.evaluate_soft_delete
Likely follow-up “Why default off?” A missing row in an API window is not a deletion.
Q34Failure / recoverySomeone deletes a row from pipeline_execution_logs. What breaks?
Strong answer
Because the log is also the checkpoint, the corresponding batch looks unprocessed and would be selected again; idempotent MERGE would then make no changes. Deleting a FAILURE row has the opposite effect: nothing.
Deeper explanation
Interpretation: control tables need restricted write access.
Where in the repo silver.select_silver_work_items
Q35Trade-offsWhy unpartitioned Delta and no routine OPTIMIZE?
Strong answer
All nine Gold tables total 51.78 MiB; partitioning would create small files with no measured benefit, and the OPTIMIZE trial on the 30.3 MB fact_deficiency file rewrote nothing.
Deeper explanation
The report says to reassess when file counts and latency justify it.
Where in the repo PDF p.6; spark_finops_2026-10-25.md
Likely follow-up “Did you measure query speed?” No; that is a limitation.
Q36Trade-offsWhy rebuild Gold from the complete Silver state every run?
Strong answer
It is simple and self-healing: the result depends only on current Silver, so retries and backfills converge. At this size it takes about 217 s (Gold audit) and reads 698,750 rows.
Deeper explanation
At 100× data I would move to incremental Gold or partitioned facts.
Where in the repo gold.refresh_gold
Likely follow-up “What's the cost?” Reads everything each run.
Q37Trade-offsDaily versus hourly: what does hourly cost?
Strong answer
One observed run is USD 0.475909 at list price (1.359740075 DBU × 0.35). Hourly for a year is 8,760 × that = USD 4,168.96 plus an assumed USD 817.60 for SQL = USD 4,986.56. Daily is USD 173.71 a year. Skipping unchanged publications and refreshing BI only after Gold are the main savings.
Deeper explanation
SQL cost is an assumption, not measured.
Where in the repo PDF p.9
Likely follow-up “Is hourly useful?” CMS refresh is not hourly, so probably not.
Q38Trade-offsWhy hash keys instead of auto-increment surrogate keys?
Strong answer
A hash of the business key is deterministic: the same record gets the same key in every run and layer without a lookup table, which makes MERGE and backfills idempotent and lets Gold reuse Silver's key.
Deeper explanation
Downside: opaque keys and no ordering.
Where in the repo silver.sha256_json_columns

Where in the repo README “Phase 3 submission package”; PDF p.13
Likely follow-up “Then why submit it?” The point is the monitoring design; I would refresh before presenting.

Pure helpers such as drift.classify_csv_header and canonical_json_sha256 are testable offline and I exercised them locally.

Do not claim testing that does not exist.

Q51Hard follow-upIs the pipeline exactly-once?
Strong answer
No: it is at-least-once execution made effectively-once by deterministic keys, row hashes and MERGE. There is no cross-table transaction.

Q52Hard follow-upWhat breaks first at 100 times the data?
Strong answer
Gold: it reads all of Silver every run and runs nine unpartitioned MERGEs; the API offset paging could also race. I would partition or cluster big facts, make Gold incremental and pre-aggregate.
Deeper explanation
That is interpretation; nothing was measured at that scale.

Q53Hard follow-upIs “serious citations per 100 facilities” fair across ownership types?
Strong answer
It divides serious citations in the last 12 complete months by the number of currently listed facilities in the group, so group size and inspection frequency matter and the rating or ownership shown is today's, not at the event date. It is a screening metric, not a causal one.
Deeper explanation
The PDF's own caveat: associations with rating are not causal.

N2 · Demo rehearsal checklist

N3 · One-page revision sheet

Pipeline in six lines

  • CMS → landing Volume + manifest (SHA-256)
  • → Bronze: all strings + lineage, drift log, quarantine
  • → Silver: typed, validated, hashed, MERGE by key
  • → Gold: star schema, validate, nine MERGEs
  • → Power BI via SQL warehouse
  • Audit every step in pipeline_execution_logs

Idempotency

  • Acquire: publication key skip
  • Bronze: deterministic batch_id, replaceWhere
  • Silver: row_hash MERGE + date guard
  • Gold: hash-aware MERGE, zero mutations on retry
  • Quarantine: null-safe anti-join

Schema drift

  • Added → log + mergeSchema
  • Missing/renamed → reject file
  • Type drift → try_cast + quarantine
  • Contract in schemas.py; import-time self-check

Privacy

  • Landing/Bronze: clear text (limitation)
  • Silver: drop phone, address, location
  • Salted SHA-256 via secret() in Spark
  • Gold: runtime ban on privacy columns

If something fails

  • Download: .partial + os.replace + SHA check
  • Bronze file fails → task raises → downstream skipped
  • Gold partial → retry task 4, then refresh BI
  • Watermark moves only after reconciliation

Be ready to admit

  • No tests/CI
  • Not atomic across Gold
  • Unpartitioned; OPTIMIZE no-op
  • No map/scatter; DAX unseen
  • 53 vs 61; stale doc links
